Comparing his own Kings' Rest keys against his Paladin, the DK took slightly less damage and needed roughly half the healing at similar damage output — and his Paladin logs predate two rounds of Paladin nerfs. He calls Perseverance of the Ebon Blade a failed buff that is now just 4% DR on low uptime, and notes DK still lacks a raid buff beyond Grip and has clumsier ranged pack-gathering than Paladin.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.claim: YoDaTV demotes Prot Paladin a tier and out of his meta-contender group: the Reflection of Radiance nerf (much shorter Sentinel uptime) is 'really, really big' on top of the prior week's damage nerf, and his own log comparison put Blood DK ahead of it in everything except utility. He still rates it a strong off-meta pick with a high win rate in pug and sub-title keys.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.claim: YoDaTV calls Holy Paladin the front-runner among healers on the PTR — already the most stable healer in his groups, now getting an overall 5% healing buff, and helped as much by the surrounding meta shifting (Blood DK rising, Prot Paladin falling) as by its own tuning. He is wary of the new 4-set drawback, joking he hopes his Holy Paladin does not have to drink through the whole key.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.claim: YoDaTV keeps Prot Warrior below Prot Paladin and 'significantly worse', but hard to move out entirely: spell reflect is worth a big chunk of health on a lot of this dungeon pool's casts and Battle Shout is a real raid buff. He puts it one or two buffs away from being a decent meta contender — right now it simply does not do enough damage.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.claim: YoDaTV leaves Vengeance among his meta contenders — damage was increased, it still brings Chaos Brand — but flags its survivability as the most RNG-dependent of the tanks (Void Fall procs), noting every tank now leans on procs (Prot Paladin on resets, Blood DK on Dance of Midnight) and Vengeance most of all.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.claim: YoDaTV thinks the Flurry Strikes 4-set bug fix might make Brewmaster playable but still nowhere near its Season 1 standing, and does not expect it to be meta — the damage he has seen from it is low. He can see it being played in the same all-physical composition it gets slotted into every season.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.claim: YoDaTV does not expect Guardian to be meta next season — the damage output he has seen from bear (and Brewmaster) on the PTR is low. He keeps it outside his contender group with no tuning yet to change that.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: MadSkillzz calls the current Mistweaver build stronger than before and 'by far the best healer, like miles' — a new mastery-stacking setup that tops both HPS and DPS. He does not expect it to last: he anticipates a Morning Breeze nerf because the scaling is out of hand, but thinks even after that Mistweaver stays close to S-tier since the normal build is still good. His complaint is that Sheilun's does nothing, leaving the spec over-reliant on Rising Sun Kick. (Recorded before the 07-23 notes cut Morning Breeze by 60%.)

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: MadSkillzz says Resto Druid falls behind the other healers in Mythic+ and would currently rank Holy Priest above it. He blames the raid-versus-M+ balancing squeeze: the spec needs a substantial M+ HoT buff, but that would make it overpowered in raid, so Blizzard buffs Regrowth instead — felt, but in his view not enough — while Verdant Fusion no longer extends HoTs. He adds the usual PTR caveat that being underpowered now is the better place to be, since buffs are more likely than nerfs.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: MadSkillzz puts Discipline in the same raid-versus-M+ trap as Resto Druid: in his view Disc should have a better atonement transfer in Mythic+, but Blizzard is fighting to keep it from being overpowered in raid, so the M+ side stays held back. He treats it as a structural balancing problem rather than a tuning one.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.claim: AutomaticJak thinks Disc is in a 'much, much better spot' for next season: Void Shield was over-nerfed and atonement buffed in return, so the spec is no longer the Void Shield spam simulator it was mid-PTR (he expects a small Void Shield correction back up, since it currently shields for less than Power Word: Shield). His worries are mana generation and comp dependence — he expects Disc to struggle in high keys unless the group can cover poison dispels for it, and he expects Blizzard to keep buffing atonement while trimming Disc's direct damage.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.claim: AutomaticJak reports no Holy Priest changes this week and a split profile: Oracle Holy is 'really good' and feels good in dungeons and is playable in keys now, while Archon looks better in raid and the spec overall still reads a bit too weak there. He speculates the Holy Priest developer is spread across other classes, and notes Holy Priest and Preservation are being logged more than Resto Druid on the PTR.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.claim: AutomaticJak has Mistweaver as 'still top dog' thanks to the crazy mastery build, with Holy Paladin and Resto Shaman next and Disc after that. He expects the mastery setup to be nerfed — 'it's just way too insane right now' — and hopes Holy Paladin stays highly tuned so there is somewhere to go when that lands. He also notes Mistweaver's power is conditional on melee-range uptime.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.claim: Across a Mythic raid-testing session Kalamazi names Destruction the Warlock spec he would pick universally for next tier and the class's best single-target option, and the one to play for high-end Mythic progression unless tuning changes — while calling it 'a little funky in certain areas'. He tiers it around B with the class as a whole 'very mid' and in need of buffs, and expects an aura buff if Warlocks go into the raid weak.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.claim: Kalamazi calls the Demonology pet nerfs 'pretty rough' and says he cannot see the reason for them — the spec was not excelling at anything or dominating the raid. He does not think it is unplayable, but rates it below Destruction (roughly C to Destro's B), reads it as 'pretty bad' on the fights they tested, and says it would need a real buff pass to be worth bringing over Destruction.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.claim: Kalamazi says a batch of Affliction bug fixes landed overnight that 'go pretty far', and now calls it probably the class's best Mythic+ spec — while noting that is partly because Demonology got nerfed. In raid he sees it as good but struggling on fights that are not stat-cleave based, with the single-target/AoE split still unresolved and Hellcaller's shard economy feeling bad; he wants a Wither/Felvine-style buff pass like the one Destruction got late last cycle.

takes.creator: Obli
takes.claim: Playing San'layn Unholy through a PTR +15, Obli says the buffed build 'inches ahead' of Frost as the better DK spec: the 45-second burst window is considerably stronger, and the damage people dismiss as a small Blood Beast melee buff actually lands through its Corrupted Blood AoE component. He rates single-target and especially execute as excellent (Death Coil and Vampiric Strike both gain ~30% under 35% health) but calls two- and three-target cleave 'not fantastic', and drops Soul Reaper entirely in keys for Necrotic Coil. He also warns the spec is now materially harder than live Unholy — holding seven stacks of Essence of the Blood Queen between packs depends on the tank, and dropping the buff is where San'layn falls off.

takes.creator: Obli
takes.claim: Obli reads Frost as the DK spec with the better multi-target profile in 12.1: Howling Blast, Icy Touch, Frozen Pulse and Remorseless Winter all give it decent two- and three-target cleave, and it is 'particularly good' at burst add waves where San'layn Unholy is only moderately better than Rider. His practical advice is to swap to Frost for council-style progression fights, and he confirms it will be a dual-wield season for Frost.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.claim: After testing the reworked 4-set live, AutomaticJak calls Holy Paladin 'very good right now' with 'basically all your abilities in good shape': Holy Shock is the button for moderate damage and Holy Light for heavy damage, where its higher mana cost buys free Infusion of Light procs and large healing. He reports mana feeling great in keys generally, with real mana burn only on hard boss fights in high keys, and defends the tier set's unusual added-mana-cost clause as the right design because it keeps the drawback from carrying past this tier. He says the spec is strong in raid and very good in dungeons apart from having to deal with poisons, and that he is currently leaning Paladin among healers.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.claim: AutomaticJak's read on Mistweaver drops after the Morning Breeze −60% change: he expected the heavy-mastery build to be 'dead', and testing it in a +15 found it 'still pretty powerful, but you definitely notice it was nerfed' and no longer clearly the best option. His verdict by the end of the session is that Monk is 'decent in keys now, but I think it needs to get a buff for raid — I think it's falling behind in raid right now'.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.claim: LBNinja7 rates the Resto Shaman tier set as one of the coolest in Season 2 and praises how its healing rains synergise with talents like Downpour, but says it leans heavily on the party clumping together: the passive rains the set procs are wasted when they land on an isolated ally, a gripe he compares to the melee-stacking requirement Preservation Evoker used to carry.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.claim: LBNinja7 says Disc has had a lot of Season 2 changes and fixes but still feels lacking in the Voidweaver department: Shadow Mend and the apex talent cover spot healing well and the tier set's more frequent Mind Blast restores the old rapid cooldown cycle, yet he thinks it has lost the punch that used to finish a ramp, singling out Penance's damage as 'barely moving health bars' even with Voidweaver.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.claim: LBNinja7 notes Holy Priest picked up further Season 2 buffs, especially to spot healing, and can heal through most mechanics — but argues its kit still gives no reason to bring it over Disc in Mythic+: outside of raw throughput 'they just don't bring anything else'. He frames its recurring problem as years of healing being buffed and nerfed, leaving it either in a good raid spot or nowhere.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.claim: LBNinja7 is glad Blizzard cut the Resto Druid tier-set proc from a 25% to a 15% HoT buff while buffing hots like Wild Growth, which makes the set less punishing when it does not proc — but he says the swing is still noticeable when a big healing check arrives with no proc up. He does not want more power taken out of the set (that would cost its appeal) and instead compares the problem to Resto Shaman's old Surging Totem RNG, which a guaranteed proc fixed.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.claim: LBNinja7 agrees Mistweaver is 'very good' coming into Season 2 and says the Spinning Crane Kick nerf gave it a real rotation again. His only complaint is build diversity: he is tired of effectively having one hero-talent choice, with Conduit dominant and Master of Harmony short of a reason to play it.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.claim: LBNinja7 says Holy Paladin 'has gotten a ton of love recently' and that the large Holy Shock buff has slowed down the odd no-Holy-Shock build. He is not unhappy with its current state, but thinks it lacks anything as distinctive as it once had and currently reads as 'just a whack-a-mole healer' — he wants an Ashen Hollow-style standout, particularly on the damage side, to make it stand out again.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.claim: Preservation is the one healer LBNinja7 says needs no fixing at all: he likes the direction Blizzard has taken it, calls the Season 2 tier set surprisingly well designed (the Essence Burst it generates gives a frequent powerful spot heal or damage), and singles out Flame Shaper as 'cranking damage on the PTR' — a damage-oriented, glass-cannon hero tree he thinks every healer should have.

takes.creator: Tettles
takes.claim: Asked on stream whether Moonkin's Mythic+ meta slot is really carried by Resto/Guardian Druid being meta rather than its own output, Tettles disagrees: 'Moonkin's numbers are just good — if Moonkin's damage wasn't good, then they wouldn't be meta.' He separately rates it as one of the easiest specs to play in keys, while raid demands far more cooldown planning.
takes.supersededNote: 2026-08-08: retired by the 2026-08-01 take from the same creator on the same spec and lens (creator-audit sweep).

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.claim: AutomaticJak now rates Holy Paladin one of the highest-HPS healers in Season 2 dungeons — "the best, if not second best", and "definitely S tier" on healing throughput. He argues the 4-set's 60% Holy Light mana penalty is what makes the kit whole: the no-Holy-Shock build is dead, Holy Shock is back as the mana-efficient single-target button, and mana is comfortable enough to run Beacon of Virtue in dungeons (and in some raid runs). He also likes that the drawback is bolted to a temporary tier set rather than the baseline kit, so it disappears next season. Herald and Lightsmith are both viable — Clarius told him Herald heals a little better, Lightsmith does more damage. His 07-27 follow-up short adds that this is the most caster-centric Holy Paladin he can remember, with Wings and Divine Toll feeling like mediocre cooldowns next to the Holy Light -> Infusion -> Flash of Light core.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.claim: After the Morning Breeze −60% cut on top of the earlier 8% caster-healing nerf, AutomaticJak reads Mistweaver as over-nerfed and lands it around A-ish tier for Mythic+, "maybe a little bit lower if it's going to struggle with some of the healing checks" — worse than Holy Paladin in keys and behind a lot of healers in raid, with the Way of the Serpent caster raid style feeling especially weak. He thinks Blizzard was solving a low-priority problem (making mastery a good stat), that the version from about two weeks earlier — Rising Sun Kick valuable, no forced spin-to-win, real value from Shaohao's Gift — was close to perfect, and that the spec has "the bones of very good gameplay" with haphazard numbers that need a course correction before launch.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ build dummy testing
takes.claim: Kalamazi's own M+-build dummy tests put Demonology ahead of the other two locks: roughly 130k sustained single target versus Affliction's ~110k, with near-identical baseline AoE (~380k) that climbs to 410-420k in Tyrant/implosion windows — the biggest cooldown swing of the three. He says the 20% Diabolist pet nerf still left the spec's Ruination, big-imp and axe-demon damage intact, and that "demo's not OP, it's just like aff is that bad". His ranking for 12.1 Mythic+ if it launched today: Demonology, then Affliction, then Destruction.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ build dummy testing
takes.claim: Kalamazi measures Affliction's M+-build single target at ~110k and calls the sustain outside cooldowns "abysmal … diabolically bad", pinning it on Unstable Affliction being undertuned — he wants roughly a 30% UA buff, which would also lift the tier set since it scales off baseline UA. AoE holds up at ~380k on Seed spam, and he credits the apex-talent and Dark Harvest bug fixes for a small AoE gain, but the Nocturnal Yield removal means Nightfall procs no longer give free instant Seeds, so shard economy and Agony upkeep now genuinely constrain the rotation. He ranks it second of the three for keys and says a UA buff is all it needs to be the pick.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ build dummy testing
takes.claim: Kalamazi still calls Destruction "our highest tuned spec currently in single target" — about 120k in his M+-build test, and steady rather than spiky — but adds that all three lock specs are subpar in single target versus other classes. In AoE it lands around 360-370k and is the hardest of the three to actually reach, because Mayhem keeps proccing on the main target or on low-health mobs; he says players have asked for two years to have Mayhem skip the primary target. He ranks it third of the three for 12.1 Mythic+ and describes the gameplay as sustaining one number rather than anything engaging.

takes.creator: Dalaran Gaming
takes.claim: Dal reads Assassination as looking genuinely good for Season 2: a 6% damage buff, a 15% buff to Implacable's fourth-strike component, and tier-set buffs pushing the double-poison build (Deadly Poison giving +10% blade damage, Amplifying Poison auto-attacks 2% -> 3%). It is testing really well in Mythic+ and feels strong to play. His reservation is gameplay, not power: making Implacable's rank 1 passively restore energy freed the spec from a Vendetta-macro workaround, but rank 3 is weak enough that theorycrafters expect to drop the fourth Apex point entirely, leaving a build of flat damage passives with no new decisions.

takes.creator: Dalaran Gaming
takes.claim: Dal rates the Outlaw changes as solid mechanical wins: Killing Spree no longer wastes over-capped combo points (they now add 15% damage per point instead of duration), it drains 20% faster inside Dread Rush without losing damage, and it skips targets with 5%+ damage reduction or immunity. Audacity now grants +80% Ambush damage passively and Subtlety Dispatch is up 15-30% (plus 50% under Between the Eyes), which makes an "Ambush build" viable on damage. But he is clear it does not restore the old Ambush playstyle — Ambush is just a stronger Sinister Strike proc, not a Vanish/Dance rotation — and the strongest new M+ build may sacrifice the Apex talent, the same passivity problem he flags for Assassination.

takes.creator: Dalaran Gaming
takes.claim: Dal says Blizzard has put Subtlety "back into a bit of a disaster spot". The only recent help is a Goremaw's Bite pass — more direct and bleed damage plus 20% of finisher damage repeated as Shadow split across affected enemies — which he measures at roughly a 2% overall damage buff, "okay, just not quite powerful". He calls the spec's tuning "pretty abysmal" and notes it is barely represented in PTR Mythic+ logs compared with its Season 1 popularity: "everybody almost forgot that Subtlety exists in Season 2". He caveats that tuning is still weeks from final, so he is judging the direction rather than the final numbers.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: MadSkillzz says Holy Paladin is "way stronger than it is on live" and that it could be a Holy Paladin season. He totals a 5% healing increase, a 50% Holy Shock buff and roughly 12% of other HPS gains, and reads the 4-set's added Holy Light mana cost (he notes the live PTR value is 50%, not the 60% in the notes) as barely a downside — running double Beacon he sat at ~90% mana all key, so he would almost call the change a net buff. He particularly likes the Lightsmith + Beacon of Virtue build, where Holy Armaments feed Holy Power spenders, and flags Blood DK + Holy Paladin as a comp with real synergy since the tank needs little sustained healing.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: MadSkillzz walks back his "by far the best healer" call after the Morning Breeze −60% nerf killed the mastery/Rising Sun Kick build he had been championing — that build let him triple a Resto Druid's damage and roughly double its healing. Re-testing both the mastery build and the traditional Shaohao's build, he lands on "I still think Monk is strong, I'm just not sure whether it's S tier", says people are downplaying it a bit, and calls the 8% cuts to Shaohao's Gift and Vivify probably too much. He now puts Mistweaver in a three-way contest with Holy Paladin and Resto Shaman rather than out in front.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: MadSkillzz expects Resto Shaman to be meta in Season 2 and names Totemic Resto Shaman in a full physical melee team as something he thinks will be very hard to beat. He judges the recent Resto Shaman rework as mattering more for raid (Riptide uptime) than for keys, and his standing complaint is variance rather than power: the spec stacks RNG from the tier set, Ascendance and the storm totem. He lists it alongside Holy Paladin and Mistweaver as the three current M+ contenders.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: MadSkillzz calls Resto Druid "the biggest loser by an absolute mile" of the 12.1 healer passes. Gameplay-wise Verdant Infusion no longer extends HoTs and the Apex talent is now proc'd by Swiftmend instead of consuming Soul of the Forest, which he says takes ages to re-learn, and he says the spec has to work ten times harder than anyone else for damage. The Abundance rework also rewrites its raid pattern: banking 10+ stacks before a Regrowth is gone, and holding five stacks is nothing. He now rates Holy Priest above Resto Druid in keys.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: MadSkillzz names Holy Priest "the biggest slept on healer right now … by quite a bit of a margin", pointing at the stack of buffs it has taken relative to live, and says he would put it above Resto Druid for Mythic+ as things stand. He stops short of a meta call — his top group stays Holy Paladin, Resto Shaman and Mistweaver — but flags it as the spec people are undervaluing going into Season 2.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: MadSkillzz thinks Discipline "could be really fun to play" in Season 2 but is held back by two fixable things: mana and atonement throughput. He says mana is a genuine issue even when he takes a pet, and that running Oracle without Mindbender leaves Shield Discipline as his only real return; he wants more atonement transfer so Disc's AoE healing feels better. He does not place it among his Mythic+ contenders.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list
takes.claim: Ranks Mistweaver top healer for S2 M+ but deliberately S, not S+: the PTR data showing another head-and-shoulders gap is 'a PTR mistake' — the nerfed Spinning Crane Kick no longer sets them apart the way S1 did, though buffed mastery/Rising Sun Kick (healing near a Sheilun's per press) keeps them the top dog.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list
takes.claim: Holy Paladin is his #2 and 'one Mistweaver nerf or one buff away' from the top meta pick: the tier set enables a three-punch spot-heal combo (Holy Light → two guaranteed Infusions → double giga Flash of Light) that's massive outside cooldowns, stacked buffs have quietly compounded, and unlike Resto Shaman the proc is guaranteed. Notes he's rated HPal high out of PTRs before and been right.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list
takes.claim: Resto Shaman lands A: a one-trick pony whose trick (stacked Healing Rains from the tier set + downpour + passive damage) is genuinely strong, plus a utility season — the only healer purging the many annoying casts, AoE-poison dispel. But the trick is 'worse than Mistweaver's last trick' and it leans on unguaranteed procs.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list
takes.claim: Disc is his #4: before the Void Shield nerfs he'd have put it above Resto Shaman — the nerf is noticeable — but atonement passive healing, strong Shadow Mend (no proc-fishing needed), and fast Mindbender cycling keep Oracle disc 'really strong'; mana (stopping a push group to drink) is what drags it down.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list
takes.claim: Preservation is his sleeper: the new tier set makes formerly-dead setup globals (Echo, Temporal Anomaly) fire strong Living Flames so 'every global feels impactful', damage is overlooked, and Rewind is still the best healing cooldown — but it's a jack-of-all-trades that Mistweaver mostly just outclasses, lacking a unique reason for high keys.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list
takes.claim: Resto Druid near the bottom: the abundance cap (from ~96% bonus crit to 50–60%) 'has felt so punishing', the kit was balanced around a since-nerfed tier set, and Convoke without Nature's Swiftness sometimes whiffs into Moonfires — 'sprinting at a Mistweaver's jog' for similar throughput with far less damage. Expects Resto Druid to be an early buff candidate.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list
takes.claim: Holy Priest is his bottom pick: it loses the throughput war to the healers above it AND to its own sister spec (Disc spot-heals better), perma-ramping flash-heal/PoH spam with no payoff; 'why would I bring a holy priest to a key… there's honestly no answer' beyond apotheosis — he wants a kit identity change, not another blanket buff.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.claim: 'Caster Holy Paladin is here': the tier set's guaranteed Infusion on Holy Light plus the 2pc's doubled infusion flash heals makes it the most caster-centric HPal he can remember — high on-demand output whenever needed, with Beacon of Virtue + Moment of Compassion synergy; the flip side is Wings and Divine Toll feel like mediocre cooldowns.
takes.supersededNote: 2026-08-08: retired by the 2026-08-01 take from the same creator on the same spec and lens (creator-audit sweep).

takes.creator: Baze
takes.claim: Baze — normally a Fury player who has disliked Arms since BFA — says this is the best Arms has felt in a very long time on the 12.1 PTR. He credits two Slayer changes: the Sudden Death proc chance raised from 15% to 25%, and a new talent (Tactical's Edge) granting a free Sudden Death proc on Colossus Smash, which turns the spec into a genuinely execute-centric, much faster-paced rotation (three Bladestorms inside Avatar, two inside a Colossus Smash window). He also notes Arms is no longer rage-starved or dependent on a Shaman for resources, and that in a +15 Blinding Vale his damage breakdown had Execute first 'by a mile' ahead of Bladestorm and Reap the Storm — adding that even if the numbers get nerfed, the gameplay loop alone is worth the pick.

takes.creator: Tettles
takes.claim: Asked on stream whether Season 2 is a 'Moonkin tier', Tettles gives a more guarded read than his mid-July one: he thinks the spec may well get nerfed again, and says that after the first round of nerfs it no longer looked insane in raid — but he still puts it among the top couple of specs. In the same stretch he reads the wider PTR board as unusually crowded (Marksmanship Hunter possibly the top DPS on logs; Moonkin, Arcane Mage, Arms Warrior and Elemental Shaman all looking good), and notes he barely engages with the tier set while playing.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: Drops Mistweaver to A tier in his retested M+ list. The mastery-stacking Morning Breeze / Rising Sun Kick build he had been calling S+ (Mistweavers doing 90–100k damage in keys with the healing to match) is dead after Morning Breeze effectiveness was cut 60%, on top of the ~8% overall healing nerf. Back on a normal stat priority it still felt quite strong on both damage and healing, but he calls the Sheilun/Vivify part of the toolkit weak and expects Blizzard to revisit it — which is why he no longer puts it in S.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: His biggest riser: high A tier, and he says some people would put it in S. Holy Shock healing +50% and its cheaper mana finally killed the no-Holy-Shock build, and the 4-set now carries what he thinks may be the first outright negative tier-set clause (Holy Light mana cost +60% in the notes, closer to 50% datamined) offset by a 5% healing increase. He reads that trade as good: you save Holy Light for emergencies and always have a button, and the spec's gameplay is simply better for it. Lightsmith with Beacon of Virtue pleasantly surprised him and he thinks he had been sleeping on it. Stays A only out of cautious optimism.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: Keeps Resto Shaman where it was (A tier) and says he could nitpick it into S. He is explicitly happy about the tier-set nerf: the spec has too much of its power sitting in RNG (tier set, Ascendance and Stormstream procs), so moving power out of the set and into the baseline toolkit is the right direction. Farseer's Chain Heal buffs made that tree feel decent, but Totemic in a full physical-melee composition felt really great, and he would be surprised if Totemic Resto is not part of that comp in Season 2.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: Calls Preservation the biggest underdog and most underappreciated healer on the PTR — healing is there, damage is absolutely there, and he likes the tier set (mostly tested Flame Shaper, plus an Emerald Blossom / Fluttering Seedlings build). But he separates that from the meta question and answers it himself: probably not meta, because it is harder to pilot, has range limitations and no good raid buff. Held at its existing placement.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: The healer that falls in this update — down to a new B+ row, because he admits he was generous in last week's ranking before testing most of the builds. A week focused on Oracle left mana still an issue and, more importantly, he wants more Atonement transfer in the panic moments: every healer above Discipline gave him an easier time in the same keys. He thinks a couple more tuning passes could make it climb, and that Blizzard is nervous about tuning it for M+ without breaking raid.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: Held in place. The Abundance / Regrowth buffs and the Abundance crit bug fix landed, but he still wants further M+ buffs, and calls Wildstalker Resto's damage quite low — partly because there is no time to apply bleeds when the healing demand is that high. He also misses Verdant Infusion no longer extending HoTs and says he is jealous of the HoT-extension talent Resto Shaman just got. Expects Blizzard to keep buffing it, but flags that as speculation.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: Stays around B tier. He is clear that Holy Priest is not bad and can push decently high keys, and the Oracle buffs (Premonition of Insight, Prayer of Mending) landed, but the currently popular dual-Oracle build leaves him with few healing buttons for his taste, its damage sits on the low end, and he wants significant — including gameplay — changes he is not holding his breath for.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: Softens yesterday's drop after retesting both builds post-Morning-Breeze. The mastery-stacking build is 'a lot weaker' but still playable; on base mastery he found Rising Sun Kick weaker and Spinning Crane Kick better, spinning to win at roughly five targets, and he personally preferred that normal build for large trash. A post-nerf normal-build log he pulls up does 61k damage — 'not the worst, not the best', a bit above average, against the ~100k the mastery build used to reach. His summary is that monks are not bad after the changes at all; the real drag is spot healing, with Vivify and Sheilun's Gift feeling like they do very little. He expects Blizzard to buff Sheilun's and for Monk to climb back a bit.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: Firms his ranking up from 'high A, some would say S' to naming Holy Paladin the front runner for the best healer of the first four or five weeks of Season 2, and putting it in S tier alongside Resto Shaman — with the distinction that Resto Shaman earns its slot inside the melee/physical comp while Holy Paladin 'looks to be just good in any' comp. He caveats that hotfixes are still landing and a lot will change after those first weeks.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: A raid-side read to go with his M+ one: Resto Shaman 'is looking way better' in raid on the back of the latest buffs, where in Mythic+ he still frames it as a spec built for the melee/physical comp. He is openly sceptical of raid healer tier lists at this point, though — the rework only had two Mythic test bosses behind it, which he says is nowhere near enough to rank healers on.

takes.creator: Shadarek
takes.claim: State-of-Havoc snapshot going into Season 2: Aldrachi Reaver pulls clear of Felscarred — roughly 4% ahead in single target against about 1% on live — because the Felscarred package was hit from every side at once, with Inertia's damage amp cut from 18% to 12% (he considers it no longer worth running), Blind Fury's fury generation nerfed, and Immolation Aura losing both fury generation and 8% damage, while Aldrachi is largely indifferent to all three and kept its aura compensation. He expects the same pure single-target Aldrachi build to also be correct in Mythic+ (Felscarred about 3% behind), where Havoc's AoE stays mediocre but its priority and funnel damage remain, in his words, unmatched. His overall read is unenthusiastic: the shift looks to him like Felscarred being dragged down rather than Aldrachi being made genuinely good, and he expects no further changes before the season starts.

takes.creator: Shadarek
takes.claim: On the Season 2 set he is lukewarm: he rates it a decent roughly 8-9% damage overall, but calls the 2-set boring (a flat damage increase to Blade Dance and Chaos Strike, including their Metamorphosis versions, plus Essence Break) and says the 4-set actively feels bad because it forces Essence Break into every build on a cooldown deliberately desynced from the rest of the kit — you simply press it on cooldown and the window no longer lines up with anything. He also flags the 4-set bonus currently landing on the damage-over-time portion instead of the initial strike, a bug that makes it slightly stronger in single target and weaker in AoE until it is corrected.
takes.supersededNote: 2026-08-08: retired by the 2026-07-31 take from the same creator on the same spec and lens (creator-audit sweep).

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.claim: Brief short-form read on the Resto Shaman rework: he thinks Farseer "might finally be back" for Season 2 on the back of the large Riptide healing buffs, the new talent that extends Riptides off totems, and the big buff to the ancestors' Chain Heal. He expects the changes to make the spec run considerably smoother, and singles out the new raid's many spread-out encounters as the setting where Farseer should be able to compete.

takes.creator: Publik
takes.claim: Early PTR numbers: the Venomous Abyss set is worth about 6% total (5% from the 2-piece, only 1% from the 4-piece), and Archon sits roughly 15%+ ahead of Voidweaver in all forms of content — mostly on the back of Focused Outburst.

takes.creator: Whispyr
takes.claim: On the 07-21 tuning: the flat 6% damage buff is welcome, but the Implacable rank-3 buff is "kinda pathetic" and the 4-set's 3%-per-stack Amplifying Poison is merely fine — nothing changes current theorycrafting except discouraging the 4/4 apex drop, which he expects players will drop anyway.
takes.supersededNote: 2026-08-08: retired by the 2026-08-03 take from the same creator on the same spec and lens (creator-audit sweep).

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.claim: Tier-list update a week out from Season 2, with no further tuning expected before launch: YoDaTV puts Blood DK alone in S+, calling it simultaneously the highest-damage AND the tankiest tank for the first time in a very long while. He quantifies the Apex-talent bug fix — Dancing Rune Weapon was ADDING 4% damage taken per weapon instead of removing it, so with two weapons up for roughly half a dungeon the Season 2 swing is about 20% less damage taken over that stretch — layered on top of separate survivability buffs. He reads Blood as the most likely meta tank, and expects any incoming nerf to land on damage, which would leave it merely S as the tankiest tank. His own caveat: most of the top keys on the PTR are still not being done by Blood DK, and he has not personally pushed high keys on it.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.claim: Drops Prot Paladin to A+ — still 'the best tank after Blood DK', but he reads the spec as gutted by the Reflection of Radiance nerf. His accounting: the +10% DR from Blessed Hammer is roughly washed out by Sentinel dropping 15s to 12s, and then the Reflection of Radiance nerf takes another large bite because Sentinel uptime falls further. Against Blood DK it takes more damage, needs more healing and does less damage, surviving on tier placement mainly because it brings Blessing of Sacrifice. He openly hopes for a compensating buff. Honest counter-evidence he raises himself: from logs, the highest keys on the PTR are still being done by Prot Paladin, so it may yet be strong at the very top.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.claim: Holds Holy Paladin in S as the best healer going into Season 2 on pure healing — by far the best at keeping a group alive through mistakes and hard heal checks, to the point that he essentially stops seeing deaths-to-healing with one in the group. What keeps it out of S+ is damage, which is noticeably low on the Herald of the Sun healing build and unhelped by the lack of a raid buff. He flags the failure mode explicitly: if a dungeon's wall turns out to be damage rather than survival, a lower-healing/higher-damage healer like Resto Shaman or Mistweaver could take the slot. He also notes the healer damage spread is far tighter than Season 1's Mistweaver blowout. Self-declared caveat: he is not a healer player and is reading from group outcomes.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.claim: Places Retribution in A+ after playing alongside several Ret Paladins on the PTR: the damage is 'actually really good', but he reads the spec as still carrying its Season 1 gaps — slightly squishier than the genuinely tanky DPS classes, and no damage-oriented raid buff to justify the slot in a meta comp. A brief placement inside a broad tier-list rundown rather than a hands-on deep dive.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.claim: Keeps Vengeance in A+ and sums it up as 'one buff away'. On damage he is positive — Annihilator is doing well and, counting Chaos Brand, he rates it roughly on par with Blood DK; he tested Ultrakill and measured it about 30% behind, so he advises against that build. Two caveats carry the mixed read: survivability and especially self-healing are well short of Blood DK, and outside Metamorphosis — tanking on Fiery Brand with no meta up — the spec genuinely needs external healing. He also flags a live Void Fall Meteor double-proc interaction (Spirit Bomb into Soul Cleave) that, if fixed, would make the damage considerably worse.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.claim: Rates Brewmaster in A — his 'playable in weird comps, but not meta' band. His read is narrow but consistent: damage is a bit low, while survivability is good enough to hold up in very high keystones. He notes with interest the one group that reliably runs Brewmaster plus Resto Shaman every season and expects them to make it work again.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.claim: Drops Guardian to A, calling bear 'pretty nerfed since last season'. He believes there is still a playable build that mirrors the Season 1 one with Mangle in place of the Thrash/Wildfire pairing, and that it remains genuinely tanky — but the damage is very low, single target especially, so he does not see it reaching the meta. He rates it perfectly playable rather than bad.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.claim: Leaves Prot Warrior in A, in essentially the same place he had it in Season 1 — with one situational upgrade: Spell Reflect is unusually valuable across the Season 2 dungeon pool. He points to reflectable casts scattered through the new pool (the large mob upstairs in Ruby Life Pools is his worked example) as free, sometimes substantial, priority damage. Not a meta call — a same-placement read with a new upside.

takes.creator: Obli
takes.claim: A full hands-on Mythic+ run on the San'layn Blightfall build, which he says has now pushed ahead of Rider as the Unholy pick. His damage read is deliberately deflationary: he finishes the key around 360-400k overall and states flatly that Unholy is 'definitely not OP' and that Arms Warrior does the same damage — rejecting the S-tier framing outright. Single target from Blightfall he calls okay but not stellar, and he highlights a structural weakness in the 45-second cadence: one Dark Transformation window including the consumed Blightfall is worth only about 120k DPS, because Unholy has nothing else on that timer (he thinks Frost's 45-second window is clearly better). He also warns the build is group-dependent — his own numbers were inflated by Shaman mastery, Havoc's magic-damage buff and Power Infusion, and in a fast-clearing key with a top-tier pilot he could not ramp at all. Build notes: Blightfall scales with Soul Reaper for a 20% bonus worth actively lining up; take Desecrate over the Death and Decay Vampiric Strike proc talent. He calls this the hardest version of DK to play by a distance, and is withholding a written guide because he does not consider the build solved yet.

takes.creator: Obli
takes.claim: Reading the 08-01 tuning pass, Obli argues that what looks on paper like an AoE nerf is in practice a single-target buff. The listed cuts are real but modest — Virulent Plague -10% (he measures it as roughly 24m down to about 2.5m lost), graveyard -15% and Epidemic -12% — while auto-attack damage doubling only moves melee from about 2% to 4.4% of his damage on a dummy and stays near 2% in a key, which he reads as a deliberate nudge to stop playing Unholy as a pseudo-ranged spec. The change he credits for the real gain is Corrupted Blood / withering grasp +25%, which also helps AoE. He points to the single-target dummy leaderboard now filling with 07-31 and 08-01 parses where it had been stale June logs, says his own keys feel slightly better than before, and calls the net effect a buff — while explicitly rejecting the S-tier framing some are giving it and placing the spec at 'A plus'. He notes Blood's San'layn nerfs do not touch Unholy's San'layn, and that Frost was left unchanged.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.claim: Rates Arms the best DPS going into Season 2, top of his S tier. He does not claim it tops every dungeon — he expects it to lead at lower target counts — but credits great funnel, single target that is 'no longer terrible', and strong two-target cleave he thinks is unusually relevant in the new pool. He also rates it genuinely tanky, singling out Spell Reflect as disproportionately good in Season 2 (reflecting the dog back on the boss in Altar of the Fangs, reflecting the elementals upstairs in Ruby Life Pools for large priority damage). He pre-empts the obvious objection — Arms could already do this in Season 1 — by arguing the three Season 1 meta DPS were outliers that have since been reined in (Unholy DK's Cycle of Death, Augmentation carrying three players through a key, an overtuned Devourer), while Arms itself gained single-target damage and what he considers a very good tier set. Attributed after Riley widened his Warrior scope from Protection-only to Protection + Arms on 2026-07-31.

takes.creator: Shadarek
takes.claim: Sims the 07-31 Havoc pass at roughly +3.6% for Aldrachi Reaver (about 235.6k to 244k) and +4.8% for a Fel-Scarred build that drops Deflecting Dance (about 230k to 241k), narrowing the gap between the two hero trees from almost 6k DPS to about 3k. He builds those numbers from the 6% added to Blade Dance, Death Sweep, Chaos Strike and Annihilation — roughly 32% of Aldrachi's damage against about 49% of that Fel-Scarred build's — plus the 12% Hunt buff and the Essence Break increases. He deliberately discounts the Essence Break gain because the sims still model the 4-set amplifying the damage-over-time portion rather than the initial strike, and he reads the unusually large secondary-damage buff as a sign Blizzard is about to fix that bug. His conclusion is that Havoc now lands in a genuinely good spot and comes within striking range of Devourer, while his standing playstyle complaint is unchanged: Eternal Hunt's 12-second window is never worth holding The Hunt for, so roughly 40% of Hunt casts buff no Eye Beam at all.

takes.creator: Shadarek
takes.claim: Calls the Eradicate secondary-target cut overdue and correct: he argues Eradicate should never have dealt full damage to off-targets, and notes Blizzard separated the main- and secondary-target values back in the .5 patch specifically so they could be tuned apart and then left them identical. He reads the 15% cut as a very significant nerf to Devourer in cleave and AoE, landing hardest on the Void's Guard build. The paired Annihilator change — Final Hour's Voidfall bonuses persisting 6 seconds instead of 8 — he did not expect and cannot account for, noting it costs uptime on both the 3% haste and the damage reduction, so the build comes out weaker and squishier at once. He still places Devourer a bit above 250k in sims, ahead of the freshly buffed Havoc builds.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.claim: Testing the 07-31 tuning pass live (Soul Fire +45%, Chaos Bolt +5%, Havoc 60%→50%), Kalamazi calls Destruction the strongest Warlock spec for single-target damage "by a decent margin" and says he would play it on most raid fights this tier; his own session averages put Destro around 153-155k against roughly 146k for Demonology and 144k for Affliction. He argues the Havoc trim was unnecessary given the Chaos Bolt buff, and stresses the read is provisional because most of the specs above Warlock were nerfed in the same pass.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.claim: Kalamazi reads the Shadow Bolt +45% / Demonbolt +55% / Summon Gloomhound +35% package as a substantial single-target buff that likely pushes Demonology back into a Sacrificed Souls build, and finds implosion builds edging out Power Siphon ones in his dummy tests. His sims have Soul Harvester slightly ahead of Diabolist. He ends the session with Demonology and Affliction close together but still behind Destruction, and notes the buffs are almost entirely single-target so they do not change the spec's cleave profile.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.claim: Kalamazi treats the Haunt buff (damage-dealt modifier 12%→16%) as a real but insufficient single-target fix for Affliction — he wanted a direct Unstable Affliction buff instead and says a 4% effective aura bump "isn't going to do much" for the spec. He does credit it with adding some funnel damage on the UA target and expects Affliction to be worth playing on a handful of seed-spam fights in the raid, but still ranks it below Destruction and roughly level with Demonology.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.claim: Playing keys after the tuning pass, Kalamazi puts all three Warlock specs close together in Mythic+ but leans Destruction as the pick, since its single target should stay somewhat ahead even in keys and it is "really impressive in mass AoE" with the Diabolist package. He is explicit that the gap is small and that where Warlock lands depends on the several specs nerfed in the same build, so he will not commit harder than "it could lowkey be Destro".

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list
takes.claim: Jak's only S-tier healer. He credits the raw output: the tier set turns Holy Light into an Infusion of Light engine (Inflorescence granting two, Judgment a 20% chance) and the 2-set doubles the healing of those Infusion-empowered Flash of Lights, while Virtue spell-queuing and Shield of the Righteous keep mana workable. He notes the post-buff Holy Shock means it is no longer a no-Shock build, and that the poison-dispel-heavy dungeon pool (six of eight) plus bleeds make Cleanse Toxins and Blessing of Protection unusually valuable. His own caveat: no raid buff and low personal damage, so if another healer is tuned to comparable output while bringing Skyfury or Mark of the Wild, Paladin can fall off the list.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list
takes.claim: A tier, and the top of it. Despite the Farseer buffs he still finds Totemic better in most dungeons — Farseer's single-target healing is good but the niche rarely gets realised when AoE healing is what the pull demands. He likes the tier set's extra Healing Rains stacking with Downpour and Acid Rain, especially in melee comps where everyone is inside them, but rates the raw output clearly below Holy Paladin (good AoE, weak single target) and calls the gameplay unexciting with no new resource or Apex interaction. Skyfury and Poison Cleansing Totem are what keep it high.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list
takes.claim: He argues the attempt to force mastery into a good position broke the spec: buffing mastery while nerfing the Forecaster-side caster healing made the Rising Sun Kick / Ancient Teachings build dominant, and then the ~60% Morning Breeze cut removed it without restoring the rest. Conduit and Revival no longer feel like real cooldowns; Chi-Ji and Thunder Focus Tea still work but are much weaker; and the Season 1 backstop of falling back on casted healing does not function any more. His conclusion is blunt for a spec that was recently top of the list: Mistweaver actually needs buffs to get back to a good position.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list
takes.claim: B tier. Output with the Oracle setup is fine — permanent Shadow Mend access, Surge of Light discounts and Divine Aegis absorbs off crits make it reliable — but Voidweaver is too weak, and the season's biggest problem is the dispel profile: with poisons in six of eight dungeons, a group that cannot cover the dispels eats through Pain Suppression charges. Mana is better than Season 1 but still has no active regeneration (even Shadowfiend barely helps), so drinking stops are unavoidable.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list
takes.claim: C tier. He rates Oracle considerably stronger than Archon right now and says the healing output itself is genuinely good, but the spec is dragged down by cooldowns that do not feel strong (Prayer of Healing goes on the back burner without Archon's modifiers), heavy immobility, and weak Prayer of Mending. The revamped Apex turning every Serenity into a Benediction Flash Heal helps single-target but leaves it with no tool to lift the whole party at once. He credits a real niche — one of the strongest healers into rot damage — while concluding other healers are simply too well-rounded to pass up.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list
takes.claim: C tier, and his harshest read of the list. He accepts the Tranquility quality-of-life change but says everything else made the spec worse: losing the Swiftmend HoT extension and Burden of Vision leaves the HoTs feeling inert, the shift onto Clearcasting Regrowth does not compensate, and the granular control that made Resto Druid satisfying in dungeons is gone. Mastery no longer feels powerful, and outside Convoke or a trinket he does not see the output meeting the season's heal checks. He notes he has never seen Druid players this unhappy with the spec, and quotes one on stream to that effect.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list
takes.claim: He rates the healing side as fully covered — the 2-set fires a Living Flame on Essence Burst consumption, the 4-set guarantees Essence Burst off Verdant Embrace, and Flame Shaper is strong with Dream Breath HoTs plus Fluttering Seedlings triggering Consume Flame — and he is seeing 90-100k personal damage in dungeons off double Fire Breath charges. What drags it down the list is unchanged: a proactive setup cost, far more GCDs and cognitive load than other healers, and an almost non-existent raid cooldown. His framing is that Preservation mains can meet the hardest HPS checks, but the extra work buys no extra reward over an easier healer.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.claim: Pro: spot healing is much more impactful, with permanent Shadow Mend uptime supplementing Penance and shields. Con: the mana cost of leaning into Shadow Mend is real — Priest was the only healer he had to stop and drink on consistently across his PTR testing — and the season's boss design punishes its low mobility, with repeated knockback-then-run-in mechanics and fights that keep you moving. He describes the spec as a 'satisfaction factory' to play but flags mana and mobility as the two things to watch.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.claim: His original main, and he says the 12.1 version feels like home: the playstyle shifts back off Regrowth toward Rejuvenation and Wild Growth, which is repetitive but comforting, and the healing profile stays unusually flexible (spread Rejuvs for AoE, stack HoTs for spot healing). Two cons: it is more proc-reliant than other healers because so many spells are balanced around the tier-set proc, so a dry stretch forces bad cooldown usage; and it is simply low numerically on the PTR. He frames that as a good position to be in — strong in a vacuum, one numeric buff (he suggests something like 8% overall healing) away from cranking.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.claim: He reads the proc density as a pro rather than a flaw: free Healing Rains that trigger Downpour and Acid Rain, free Apex totems and free Ascendance arrive on a conveyor belt that makes the rotation feel rewarding, on top of steady passive AoE from Healing Rain and Riptide and solid Chain Heal spot healing. He calls it the safest, most cushioned healer to sit behind. Two cons: it leans on the party stacking tightly enough for spawned Healing Rains to cover everyone, which is a pug risk, and the constant proc-fishing gives it a gambling feel.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.claim: He keeps it short because of how much hype it already has: the build revolves around the spec's strongest buttons, with Holy Light generating free Infusion of Light for instant empowered Flash of Lights, and the tier set built directly around that loop. Given the mana to sustain it, he calls the burst, spot and cleave healing enormous, and Avenging Wrath plus the two instant Holy Lights from the new set 'god mode'. The best Holy Paladin season he has seen in years. His only con is the hype itself — a heavily-picked spec carries nerf risk, and he has watched a guild swap into the PTR darling and get nerfed during the race.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.claim: As a Mistweaver main he calls the dynamic rotation genuinely back — Spinning Crane Kick nerfed, Rising Sun Kick, Ancient Teachings and Jade Fire Teachings buffed — which he rates as great for the player even if it is not what makes the spec strong. On placement he is explicit that after the PTR nerfs he still has Mistweaver in S tier, moving from what he considered S+ down to S, now contested by Holy Paladin (which he says he would also raise to S having tested it more), and argues the spec is criminally underrated by the community post-nerf. The trade-off he names: it is no longer the one-button pack-healer of Season 1.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.claim: He thinks the spec is getting slightly better into Season 2 but leads with the non-gameplay problem: community perception in Mythic+ has been low long enough that it is self-sustaining, and the practical con is not getting invited. Mechanically he flags the same Priest mana and mobility issues as Discipline, and a tier set that is entirely passive (a HoT you do not apply generating a crit buff) — relaxing for a casual player, unsatisfying for a min-maxer. The pros he names are structural: the free swap to Discipline mid-season that no other healer class has, two genuinely close hero trees (he still rates Oracle stronger), and strong ramp healing that rewards banking Prayer of Mending, Lightweaver stacks and Holy Words before damage.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.claim: The spec he is most enthusiastic about — 'it just keeps winning'. Season 2 leans further into Dream Breath's HoT, and he says Flame Shaper was giga-buffed alongside it: high healer damage, and a Consume Flame that now bursts for much more. He calls it the best 'hipster' pick — not in the race for the top healer slot, but strong, and he openly says he cannot personally find cons for it while acknowledging that is a biased read and inviting the audience to name them.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list (short-form update)
takes.claim: After weeks of testing he says it is finally time to place Holy Paladin in S tier, pointing at the 07-31 buff on top of what he describes as buffs almost every single week, and concludes Paladin will be significantly better in Season 2 than it was in Season 1.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list (short-form update)
takes.claim: He frames Resto Shaman as a composition pick rather than a raw-output one: Skyfury, Bloodlust and a ranged interrupt slot it well into the physical melee comp, and if you enjoy that comp he rates it a decent choice.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list (short-form update)
takes.claim: He says Mistweaver was genuinely strong on the PTR until it was nerfed and is still a solid healer, but that its toolkit is now lacking in places and Blizzard needs to address the Sheilun's Gift / Vivify side of the kit.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list (short-form update)
takes.claim: Calls Preservation the biggest underdog healer of the season — it can put out good healing and an insane amount of damage — while naming the same two obstacles as everyone else: it is harder to play, and it has no good raid buff.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list (short-form update)
takes.claim: His ask for Discipline is specific rather than a placement call: he wants more Atonement transfer buffs aimed at Mythic+ content.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list (short-form update)
takes.claim: He says Resto Druid's damage is really not good and he would like to see further healing buffs, reading the spec as caught in Blizzard's difficulty balancing it between raid and Mythic+ at the same time.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list (short-form update)
takes.claim: Notes Holy Priest received buffs and could rise a little on his list as a result, but says he would have liked more impactful gameplay changes for it in Mythic+ rather than numbers.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR (2026-07-31 build) — Season 2 M+ tier list update
takes.claim: He puts the damage nerf at roughly 4-5% depending on target count and says it is not big enough to move Blood off the number-one tank spot: survivability was untouched, so he still reads it as the tankiest tank, and even after the cut he thinks its damage is the best of all tanks once raid buffs are counted. Blood stays in his S+ row.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR (2026-07-31 build) — Season 2 M+ tier list update
takes.claim: The 8% damage buff moves Guardian up to his A+ 'one buff away' row. Playing it himself, he found the Druid of the Claw no-Rejuvenation build about as tanky as Blood DK, but still doing less than half of a DPS's damage where Blood sits closer to 60-70%, and lower than Blood even counting Mark of the Wild. He thinks one more damage buff would make it a genuine meta contender — and adds he is not hoping for that after a season of bear.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR (2026-07-31 build) — Season 2 M+ tier list update
takes.claim: He rates Vengeance's damage as very close to Blood DK's after the Blood nerf, before Chaos Brand, but holds it out of the meta on survivability: Annihilator's cooldowns are RNG enough to make mitigation inconsistent, and Aldrachi Reaver is steadier but unplayable on damage. His read is that one defensive buff could make it meta, and it is not there yet.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR (2026-07-31 build) — Season 2 M+ tier list update
takes.claim: A tier alongside Prot Warrior: he says both can definitely survive the keys, but they require noticeably more healing than Blood DK and have to work harder while doing less damage, which is what keeps them a row below the tanks he would build a comp around.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR (2026-07-31 build) — Season 2 M+ tier list update
takes.claim: A tier with Brewmaster — survivable in keys but needing more healing and doing less damage than Blood DK. He calls the 6% damage buff in the 07-31 notes 'not nothing' but does not see it splashing Prot Warrior into the meta.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR (2026-07-31 build) — Season 2 M+ tier list update
takes.claim: He says Prot Paladin has lost its lustre since the Reflection of Radiance nerf: still tanky inside cooldowns, but cooldown uptime is now low and its damage is nowhere near Blood DK's. Without a compensation buff for that nerf he does not see it being good in the meta.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR (2026-07-31 build) — Season 2 M+ tier list update
takes.claim: He calls the extra 5% healing a head-scratcher because Holy Paladin was already by far the best throughput healer in Mythic+ and is now further ahead, and places it in his S+ row as the default healer pick on output alone. The caveat he raises is composition rather than power: a Blood DK tank plus a Holy Paladin healer is zero raid buffs, so if a Shaman or Druid healer can meet the heal checks, they may get played over it.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR (2026-07-31 build) — Season 2 M+ tier list update
takes.claim: A tier, from his own play: damage is fine under normal conditions but the spec has bad edge cases — an immune boss phase, or a fight where the one-minute cooldowns do not line up — and he rates it clearly worse than Season 1 Retribution.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR (2026-07-31 build) — Season 2 M+ tier list update
takes.claim: He reads the 07-31 pass as a very small net nerf (under ~2% single target) offset by a compensating AoE buff, and keeps Arms in S+ as the best melee in the game right now: decent single target, really good funnel, a great damage profile and a very tanky body. He notes the awkwardness that his two best DPS specs, Arms and Arcane Mage, are mutually exclusive on raid buffs — a group cannot benefit from both Battle Shout and Arcane Intellect — and wonders whether class balance ends up bad enough that you play both anyway.

takes.creator: Tettles
takes.claim: Despite the stream title, Tettles explicitly disclaims the doom read as clickbait: he puts the 07-31 nerf at around 3% and says the spec is fine, while adding he would be surprised if it ends up good in both raid and Mythic+. His substantive concern is the raid's damage profile rather than the tuning — he calls Venomous Abyss the least balanced profile he can remember, with two of the last three bosses being two-target fights, which is where Moonkin is weakest; it is good on three of the first four (Lost Explorers, Vashnik, Nek'zali), so how it fares depends on which bosses turn out to be hard. He separately notes Moonkin's burst is bottom-half of the cast even on the Convoke / Keeper of the Grove build, capping around 284k against roughly 338k for Unholy DK, so its value rests on sustained casting rather than cooldown windows.

takes.creator: Supatease
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Elemental rework read; his own testing shown is on PvP dummies and duels, with the PvE read taken from reviewing logs
takes.claim: He reads 12.1's Elemental pass as part of a game-wide move of power out of cooldowns and into baseline abilities: Ascendance was stripped down substantially and the damage redistributed, which he says shows up as much healthier sustained output. He rates the Season 2 set bonus strongly — 25% more Earth Shock / Earthquake / Elemental Blast damage, plus free empowered casts and a Maelstrom-free Earthquake when Storm Keeper or Ascendance falls off — and calls 12.1 a 'feels-good patch' for the spec. Framing caveat: the damage numbers he shows are from PvP training dummies and a duel, and he says his PvE read comes from reviewing other players' logs rather than his own PvE testing.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his Season 2 Blood DK Mythic+ guide
takes.claim: Opens his Season 2 M+ guide by calling Blood DK the best tank for Mythic+ at the start of the season on current PTR testing: the most damage of any tank (especially AoE), the best self-healing, and the steadiest health bar he has seen in high keys. He credits the buffs plus the Apex-talent hotfix that flipped the talent from INCREASING damage taken by 4% to reducing it by 6% per stack — roughly a 10% swing with one weapon active and up to ~20% with two. He recommends San'layn over Deathbringer (Blood Soaked Ground now 8% physical reduction, was 5%) for damage, calling survivability between the two close and saying theorycraft may even favour Deathbringer slightly. Versatility/Haste for M+ because defensive stats beat damage stats in keys. He rates the Season 2 tier set 'very good' but says his HPL testing shows no reason to consume the 4-set at 10 stacks off cooldown — Marrowrend when you would anyway and take the strength then.

takes.creator: Dalaran Gaming
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — walkthrough of the 2026-07-31 class tuning notes
takes.claim: Calls the 10% damage buff 'very solid, big numbers, kind of what assassination really needed', but says it does not fix the spec's actual problem: good single target, decent AoE, yet it falls behind specifically at two and three targets, where it used to have good tools and no longer does. He groups this with Outlaw and Subtlety as the same unaddressed class-wide weakness and says a lot of players were hoping Blizzard would address it in this pass and it did not.

takes.creator: Dalaran Gaming
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — walkthrough of the 2026-07-31 class tuning notes
takes.claim: Reads the 6% buff as smaller than the other two Rogue specs but still needed and welcome. Same structural caveat as the rest of the class: Blade Flurry handles wide AoE fine, but Outlaw is much weaker at two and three targets than in past expansions, and this pass did nothing about that dead zone.

takes.creator: Dalaran Gaming
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — walkthrough of the 2026-07-31 class tuning notes
takes.claim: Says Subtlety needed the buff and the 10% is good, but is unconvinced by the new reward talent Warfiend's Bite — the returning Legion artifact ability, meant to be decent at both single target and cleave, which in his view 'just doesn't accomplish that goal', leaving the spec still on the weaker side there. Shares the class-wide two-to-three-target dead zone he says Blizzard did not address in this pass.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Venomous Abyss per-boss raid outlook
takes.claim: Reads Venomous Abyss as overwhelmingly a Destruction raid: every boss except the opener looks like a Destro fight to him, and he calls it the best Warlock spec for the tier in both single target and spread cleave, with Hellcaller the build throughout and the Mayhem-vs-Havoc choice close on the multi-target bosses. He tempers it at class level though — he does not think Warlock single target is in a phenomenal spot and says there are definitely classes ahead of them, so Destro is best-of-three rather than strong outright. Expects further tuning around the week the raid opens.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Venomous Abyss per-boss raid outlook
takes.claim: Calls Affliction undertuned for the tier. After the tier-set nerf and bug fixes plus the removal of Patient Zero and Nocturnal Yield it no longer brings the single target the old full-value Unstable Affliction set did, and what is left is narrow: it works where you can spam Seed of Corruption into stacked adds (he floats it for the opening boss) rather than because dots are good, which he frames as playing the spec for the seed gimmick. Also notes it no longer has the cooldown reduction to get Dark Harvest onto the Twin Fangs back-room adds.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Venomous Abyss per-boss raid outlook
takes.claim: Places Demonology as a situational middle option: single target sims about level with Affliction (a bit either side depending on Apex RNG) and it is good at stack cleave, but pet travel time makes it awkward on the add-chasing fights, he found it clunky on Coiled Altar, and demo nerfs are landing. He floats it as a possibility on a couple of bosses without it displacing Destruction anywhere.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list (corrected)
takes.claim: Corrects his earlier ranking and drops Mistweaver a clear step below Holy Paladin, to the back of A tier. As a Mistweaver main he says the Rising Sun Kick nerf hurts less on its own than people expected — the globals still heal well for their cost — but that it exposed how little Shaluun's Gift and the spec's spot healing contribute now they are no longer hidden behind the oversized kicks. Calls it a jack of all trades, master of none, and says he has not enjoyed its PTR raid healing outside Chi-Ji.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list (corrected)
takes.claim: Ranks Holy Paladin the best healer and the lone S tier, though deliberately not S+, on survivability and large burst healing. His one reservation is composition: it brings Devotion Aura but does not amplify the Blood DK / Arcane Mage / Warrior core he says has been dominating PTR keys, the way Mistweaver or Resto Shaman can — which he thinks leaves a window open for those two in push groups.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list (corrected)
takes.claim: Moves Resto Shaman to the top of A tier as the consistent healer of the season and expects it to chisel its way into the meta composition — helped, he notes, by its raid buff being unlikely to be covered by a DPS spec in the group.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list (corrected)

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list (corrected)
takes.claim: Continues to call Preservation the healer people are not looking at — still very solid and his standing sleeper pick for the season.

takes.creator: LBNinja7

takes.claim: Defends Holy Priest as better than its reputation — he notes the recent healing buff and says it has climbed steadily from a genuinely bad early PTR — but keeps it near the bottom because of comp: he reads it as essentially a worse Disc Priest in a group.

takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — S2 M+ healer tier list (corrected)
takes.claim: Same shape as his Holy Priest read: much improved since early PTR and better than a lot of people think, but he reads it as a worse Resto Shaman in a composition, which caps where it can land. Stresses the whole list is PTR speculation and should be taken with a grain of salt.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: Reads the S2 pass as the raid-facing mini-rework competitive Resto Shamans have been waiting on: buffs to Unleash Life and Earth Shield, a substantial Riptide buff, Healing Rain now hitting up to six targets instead of five, and a new talent he says fits raid specifically. His framing is that Resto Shaman has trailed in raid for several seasons — he re-rolled off it for S1 progression — and this should finally make it worth bringing rather than a detriment to the healing comp, though he stops short of calling it race-to-world-first material. Flags the tier set as a downside: the proc-driven healing makes the spec feel like a gamble.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: Calls Preservation the most undervalued healer in M+ and the most fun spec of his S2 testing. The tier set adds spot healing or extra damage off essence spenders, Live Spark was buffed, and he rates its healer damage as bonkers — arguably the best of any M+ healer. Explicitly gated on difficulty: it is harder to play than the alternatives and the range limitations remain, so he doubts many players will swap, but says the payoff is there for those who put the time in. On the 08-03 stream he adds that he does not expect it to be meta, for lack of a good raid buff.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: The most hyped healer of the patch on his testing: Holy Shock buffed and cheaper on mana, the 4-set guaranteeing double Infusion off Holy Light, and a toolkit where the heals visibly move HP bars — which he notes is rare in S2 given the health increases. Calls it an absolute blaster in M+ and understands why others are placing it S tier. Two explicit caveats: being OP at season start historically puts a healer on the tuning chopping block, and he has barely tested it in raid, where he will only say the numbers look not bad.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: His honorable mention — he was strongly considering maining it. Says it felt genuinely fun in M+ testing and he likes the S2 changes that cut its RNG, but atonement transfer does not pay off enough in M+ for the effort the spec demands. His read is conditional: if Blizzard raises atonement transfer for M+ specifically, Discipline could be an absolute blaster; he is waiting to see whether that happens.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: On stream he pushes back on Holy Priest being written off, saying he thinks it is being underrated and that after the latest 5% buff it will be more than good enough for the content the overwhelming majority of players do. Frames his own decision not to play it as build preference — he dislikes the M+ builds it is running — rather than a power judgement, and warns viewers against dropping a healer they enjoy on the strength of a tier list.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ outlook (speculative power tier list)
takes.claim: In his speculative S2 M+ tier list he puts Resto Shaman as more likely to end up meta than Holy Paladin — not because it is stronger on current tuning (he says Holy Paladin is the best M+ healer as things stand) but because the physical melee comp looks strong next season, with Arms Warrior doing numbers, Windwalker performing well and Rogues substantially buffed, while a spec that is OP at season start invites the nerf. Stresses the whole list is PTR speculation and that any healer clears the content most players play.

takes.creator: Whispyr
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 raid utility (log A/B analysis)
takes.claim: Argues against the circulating claim that Atrophic Poison is not a real raid buff: A/B-ing rogue against non-rogue logs, he shows the 5% reduction does apply to the environmental damage on Twin Fangs and Sszorak, because that damage is quietly attributed back to the boss even though the logs do not display it that way. It genuinely fails only where damage comes from named untargetable NPCs — The Lost Explorers is the worst case, with roughly 40% of the damage unreducible. Concludes Atrophic is probably better than Devotion Aura going into the tier. Separately notes Rogue low-target cleave remains bad and that the recent 10% Assassination aura buff, while fine, does not address it — that needs targeted tuning.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 Protection Paladin M+ guide
takes.claim: His S2 guide opens by placing Prot Paladin below Blood DK on current PTR tuning, and says it is significantly worse on total survivability and external healing required. Root cause he gives is the rework losing Sanctified Wrath plus the heavy Reflection of Radiance nerf: Sentinel now covers roughly 20-25 seconds a minute instead of the 30-40 second windows of S1, leaving about 15 seconds a minute uncovered by any cooldown. His verdict is that it is defensively worse than in Season 1 despite gaining 10% DR, crit wings during Sentinel and a better damage profile. What keeps it playable is utility: near-solo interrupt coverage off Avengers Shield and Divine Toll resonance, and a one-minute Sacrifice external he calls OP for M+ since no other tank has one — a strong pug-carrying pick rather than a strong tank.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing)
takes.claim: His top healer for Season 2 raid. Disc puts out huge healing AND roughly 70k+ single-target damage through progression, which he calls enormously helpful for a race-to-world-first environment, and he notes there is no penalty for stacking two of them (Power Infusion on top). Mana is fantastic, especially on Voidweaver. He airs Klanden's caveat with it: numbers and damage are good — arguably too high — but Voidweaver play style is "ignore your Disc fundamentals and press good buttons on cooldown", Oracle is falling behind, and heavy movement hurts because Void Blast cannot be cast while moving.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing)
takes.claim: A tier. Pres "blasted tons of healing" in the testing, with the Flameshaper setup putting better emphasis on Dream Breath and Consume Flame working with both fluttering seedlings and Verdant Embrace. It looked best when the raid was hard-stacked but still did a fantastic job on a light spread, and its mana economy read as being in a good spot. He cites UT's hands-on impression of being flooded with Essence Burst procs and going well over a million HPS inside a Stasis window.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing)
takes.claim: A tier. He argues an underrated effect of the PTR's ~30% health-pool inflation is that Holy Light and Lay on Hands are no longer overweight, so the whole kit is appropriately sized to the new health bars. Output was "incredibly, incredibly high", especially on-demand spot healing. Caveat from Clarius after testing: it feels really strong when overhealing is low, hard to get value out of Virtue when other healers snipe it, and mana is a bit tight (though that should ease on a real fight where Virtue is not pressed on cooldown). He is unsure which Paladin spec ends up the race-to-world-first pick.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing)
takes.claim: B tier and the only spec there — he calls Resto Shaman the dark horse, "a tier away" from the world-first conversation. Strong when the raid can stack, and he flags Coiled Altar as a fight that should suit it (pulsing AoE plus stacking healing absorbs). The blocker is comp value rather than throughput: Harik's read, which he endorses, is that the numbers are genuinely good and mana is workable, but there is no reason to bring a Shaman as the fourth healer over a second Disc Priest unless you specifically want the Skyfury buff. One healer nerf above it would move it.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing)
