takes.claim: C tier. He tried both Oracle and Archon and says Holy Priest simply needs its passive healing to be stronger to succeed. Oracle should be favoured by a raid full of ticking rot damage and Prompt Prophecy buffs, but it was not — Archon was still stronger and is enormously bursty (Halo plus Apotheosis smashes health bars), while the gaps between cooldowns are boring and mana-starved. Every single test run ended near or at zero mana. His diagnosis: Blizzard keeps cutting Flash Heal and Prayer of Healing mana costs while removing the free casts (Surge of Light, Apotheosis Holy Words), so full-price casting still drains the bar.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing)
takes.claim: C tier. Meg tested mastery-heavy Ancient Teachings and caster Mistweaver variants across multiple cooldown and comp setups and Mistweaver struggled throughout — not out of mana, but not producing much healing either. Her read, which he presents: the caster spells do nothing, the 8% aura nerf was unneeded given the state of the other healers, and Ancient Teachings only looks better because it is damage-based and therefore untouched by the healing-aura nerf. Her conclusion is that you would not bring a Monk in any competitive situation right now.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing)
takes.claim: Bottom of the list. He says Resto Druid has been struggling through all of Season 2 PTR testing and that the quality-of-life additions have left the spec feeling worse overall. Even in the environment that should suit it — stacked raid, constant rot and ticking damage — it consistently landed at the bottom of the group's raw output, with the testing splitting into a clear winners group and losers group. Viteman's asks, which he relays: buff HoTs, rework the 4-piece (the old one that granted Clearcasting synergised better), and rebuff Regrowth.

takes.creator: Obli
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Mythic+ (hands-on Rider Frost DK, Den of Nalorakk +15)
takes.claim: Playing the Rider build through a PTR +15, Obli reads Frost as "doing pretty decent" and capable of a lot. He is enthusiastic about the Season 2 tier set — the stacking Remorseless Winter buff feeding Icy Death Torrent, which he expects to be the main damage source and which pushes crit hard while raising haste and mastery to equal secondary value — and about Rider's mobility (horse uptime) covering a long-standing Frost weakness. Build space narrowed: Icy Death Torrent and Obliteration are locked, so it is Breath or Frostbane, and he recommends Breath for consistency over Frostbane's RNG. His reservation is the hype: despite sims and DK-community talk that Frost will be much better than Unholy, he says single target "hasn't been anything outstanding" and there are better single-target options. Where he does back it is low-target cleave, which he expects Frost to be king of while Unholy lags.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Warlock single-target sims (Warlock Discord APLs), raid lens
takes.claim: Destruction is the highest-simming Warlock spec in single target — roughly 222k on Hellcaller against 215k on Diabolist — and he expects it to be the most-played Warlock spec in the raid this tier. He is careful that 222k is not a high number in absolute terms (he points to specs simming 250-270k), so the case for Destro is its toolkit rather than its raw sim: he calls Warlock one of the best spread-cleave classes in the game and reads five of the seven tested Venomous Abyss bosses as Destro fights — four good Havoc/Mayhem cleave fights plus Sszorak, where Destro is the best Warlock single-target option. Soul Fire's 45% buff last week locks in the build; the Destruction capstones went untouched this patch and he still calls that pathing a mess.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Warlock single-target sims (Warlock Discord APLs), raid lens
takes.claim: After the ~20% Diabolist pet-damage nerf and the following Shadow Bolt / Demon Bolt / Gloomhound buffs, Soul Harvester now sims about 7k above Diabolist in pure single target (~211k). He still expects Diabolist to be the spec played in the raid: he ran a five-target one-minute comparison and Diabolist came out far ahead (765k vs 548k) on an Implosion / Hell back build, and he reads Venomous Abyss as a cleave meat grinder where the single-target edge rarely pays. His overall class-level read is that Demonology has been 'exceptionally mid' this cycle and that other classes power-crept past Warlock.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Warlock single-target sims (Warlock Discord APLs), raid lens
takes.claim: His bluntest read of the three: Affliction 'is not good'. Last week's 4% Haunt modifier buff helped a little and he agrees Haunt is the right lever (it scales every damage source, not just Unstable Affliction), but it was nowhere near enough — Soul Harvester sims ~205-206k and Hellcaller ~200k, which he calls a disaster when other specs are at 250k+ and some as high as 270k, a 20-30% gap. He wants a Hellcaller fix along the lines of the Flamevine/Malevolence intervention Destro got days before last tier's raid opened. Talent structure is a second complaint: the tree forces a pure single-target or pure AoE build with no middle, and Ashen Curse being played on both builds papers over that rather than fixing it.

takes.creator: Shadarek
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Devourer sims corrected after a double-haste GCD bug was found
takes.claim: Explains the long-standing gap between Devourer sims and live play: because many Devourer abilities are ports of Havoc ones, haste was being applied to the GCD twice, so Devour (a 1.25s cast with Improved Consume) effectively lost its post-cast gap and the spec got extra casts at high haste. With the interaction modelled and no other changes, Annihilator single target went 214k to 245k — from 15% behind Void-Scarred to 10% — and with early APL optimisation to about 250k single target and 231k on an AoE/dungeon build, cutting the dungeon-route gap to roughly two-thirds of what it was. He concludes both Devourer builds now sim flat out ahead of Havoc in every way and ahead of most specs in the game, and reads it as explaining why Annihilator was already overperforming its sims on PTR logs. Two caveats he states himself: this is a live game bug he thinks Blizzard should fix before the tier starts, so the strength is contingent on it surviving; and it raises haste's value sharply up to a breakpoint where the GCD bottoms out.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 Vengeance DH Mythic+ guide
takes.claim: Opening his Season 2 Vengeance guide he calls the spec 'looking really strong going into next season' on the strength of its damage and its raid buff, but explicitly declines to call it the meta tank because its defensives are RNG-dependent. The damage read rests on Annihilator, which he recommends outright over Aldrachi: he rates the two about equal defensively and close on Metamorphosis uptime, so Annihilator's higher damage decides it. He flags that the current Annihilator rotation runs on a bug — holding Spirit Bomb and casting it into Soul Cleave on the same Voidfall proc fires six meteors instead of three — which makes Spirit Bomb otherwise unused, and he notes nobody has pushed high keys as VDH yet so the build is unsettled. His two practical Season 2 warnings are that Fiery Brand and Metamorphosis are both offensive and defensive buttons that cannot be spent purely for damage in keys, and that the Sigil-of-Flame-centred tier set makes trash gathering awkward because a partial-hit sigil is a large damage loss.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ Guardian Druid guide
takes.claim: His Season 2 Mythic+ bear guide. He calls Guardian definitely one of the tankiest tanks with a genuinely valuable utility package — Mark of the Wild as a raid buff, decurse and remove poison, and Stampeding Roar, which he singles out as very strong for the indoor Season 2 dungeons — and expects the new Thrash/Mangle priority to generate far more Ironfur than Season 1, holding armor capped around 85% through Incarnation. His one reservation is damage, which he calls a little bit low especially in the Mythic+ build, and that is why he says it is not the meta tank — while still calling bear pretty strong going into next season and saying he would not be surprised to see it meta again if it picks up more damage buffs. He also warns that Lunar Beam is no longer a real defensive under Druid of the Claw (roughly 10% mastery and much less self-healing than before), leaving Barkskin, the 15% damage reduction from Ravage's Dreadful Wound, and roughly one Survival Instincts charge per Incarnation — with the caveat that even at that rate you run low later in a dungeon.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 raid testing (Atonement structural review with Clandon of WarcraftPriests)
takes.claim: He opens by saying Disc is doing incredibly well in Season 2 testing — off a Dummy Dome session that day he calls it one of the strongest healers and doing absurd amounts of damage — but that it also has really big structural problems. Working through a scaling chart Clandon built, Atonement is flat for the first five targets and then falls off a cliff: 5 to 6 adds 4.66% healing (the largest gain left on the curve), the 15th to 16th adds 1.63%, and fifteen extra Atonements together buy only about 41% more healing. The consequence they draw is that high Atonement counts now purchase coverage rather than throughput, so raid play becomes a haste-stacked rotation — Mind Blast proccing Void Shield to cut its RNG, the tier set looping Penance into Mind Blast cooldown reduction, Radiance cycling on smart targets — rather than the classic ramp, and output goes close to binary: near-flat HPS instead of the old spikes, with little granularity between doing all your healing and none. They do carve out exceptions — Ultimate Penitence is still huge because Void Infusion adds 75% to Penance healing inside the rift, and a heavy-movement fight could break the pattern — they revisit whether you can stand still long enough to benefit from Voidweaver at all, and note that losing Greater Smite stacks to forced movement has a real, if not catastrophic, effect on immediate healing. On damage Clandon measured roughly 78-80k in their pulls, and reckons that even halving it to 38-40k would still be three to four times any other healer. Jak's closing question is how Blizzard nerfs that without ruining Disc for a race-to-world-first environment; Clandon expects no structural fix before the patch ships.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ outlook (Atonement structural review with Clandon of WarcraftPriests)
takes.claim: On the Mythic+ side he is blunt: his own Voidweaver testing in keys feels awful right now — a moderate level of healing all the time, with no way to push health bars up quickly the way a rift-up Voidweaver could last expansion. Clandon supplies the structural reason: because Atonement output is effectively always maxed, Disc has no lever left to pull, so the season starts fine through the low keys and then hits the level where gear stops keeping up with key scaling and Atonement is simply no longer enough — with Shadow Mend significantly weaker than the previous proc version (more consistent, but no longer the emergency punch), Void Shield's power shifted out of raw absorb into Atonement application, and nothing beyond Shadow Mend spam and a couple of Pain Suppression charges to fall back on. Clandon's proposed fix is a hybrid rather than scrapping the scaling: soften the curve and restore a reduced version of the retired out-of-raid Atonement bonus — he floats 30-40%, where it was 100% historically and then 75% before being cut — so keys can be tuned without breaking raid. Jak endorses the shape of it, saying a single front-end number would make a huge difference for Disc in keys.

takes.creator: Sha
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — review of the official 12.1 patch notes; Season 2 Mythic+ outlook
takes.claim: Reviewing the official 12.1 notes as the final word barring minor tuning, he reads Brewmaster as ending the PTR cycle in a rough spot. His central objection is Celestial Brew/Celestial Infusion: absorb up 50% but cooldown up 100%, a change datamined weeks earlier and never given a dev note. He reads the intent as making Infusion a real tank-buster answer (a fair goal, since he felt Brewmaster was at its weakest in raid all of Season 1 after losing Zen Meditation, Diffuse Magic and its larger absorbs), but the cost is the Apex 'Bring Me Another' feedback loop: Infusion had become the rotational catalyst, and halving its frequency leaves a resource deficit gated on a 20% Purifying Brew proc, so unlucky streaks leave you with no brews, no energy and nothing to press for several seconds. He says it pushes you toward Black Ox Brew and Master of Harmony as a resource safety net and leaves Shadowpan clunky. On the tier set he is blunter: measured over a four-minute Altar of the Storm test the four-piece is 10% of his damage and the two-piece 1%, and the four-piece damage requires mobs to stand in a small ground patch — unrealistic in keys with kiting and gathering, unlike every other tank set which keys off abilities. If Brewmaster is tuned around a sim assuming full uptime on that patch, he expects it to underperform. He also flags that Vivify was left to scale poorly against the +25% max-level health, at roughly 2% of his own health bar, removing the tank's ability to help keep a group member alive. Bottom line for players asking whether to main it: defensively it is fine (he had no trouble on PTR 18s and 19s), but it will not do much damage and does not bring much, so anyone on the fence should swap back to another tank; Brewmaster stays viable specifically as the physical-composition filler alongside the likes of Arms, Outlaw, Feral and Resto Shaman.

takes.creator: VooDooSaurus
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Devourer and Havoc sim pass after a haste/GCD double-apply bug was found and corrected in the sims
takes.claim: He reports what he calls the strangest find of his theorycrafting career: since Devourer's alpha release, haste has been double-applying to the GCD of Reap, Cull, Consume and Devour in game, so those GCDs reached the 0.75s floor at 50% haste rather than 100%. The sims never modelled it, which is why sim output had persistently undershot in-game results. With the behaviour now reproduced, Void Scourge sims around 275k single target and he says plainly that Devour is broken and insanely busted — Void Scourge stays the raid build with roughly a 20k single-target gap over Annihilator, and even Void Scourge's dungeon/cleave build out-single-targets Annihilator's pure single-target build. The read is explicitly provisional in both directions: he has reported the bug and says it either gets fixed, in which case the older sims were right, or Blizzard aura-nerfs the spec, which is what he hopes for; his stated fear is an aura nerf applied without the bug fix being compensated. He also notes Annihilator gained more from the correction than Void Scourge (about 7% across scenarios) because Metamorphosis uptime yields more Collapsing Stars, so a bug fix would hit Annihilator hardest — while Collapsing Star itself is weak enough that building around extra stars is no longer worth it.

takes.creator: VooDooSaurus
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Havoc sim pass ahead of Season 2 (sims run with Shadarek, Azortharion and Sailor)
takes.claim: Alongside the Devourer numbers he puts Havoc in a strong spot for 12.1. Aldrachi is the raid build and now posts what he calls a genuinely good single-target number — he is careful to say it reads well on its own terms even next to Devourer's inflated figures — and the same build carries into AoE. The Felscarred single-target build he dismisses as an atrocity you will rarely play: it gives up the Blade Dance shield, a meaningful Apex defensive, and lacks cleave. Havoc's defining strength in his read is funnel: roughly 11% of its damage on single target and 14-15% once you scale to five and eight targets comes from funnel, and he expects priority and funnel damage to be valuable in this season's dungeons. The honest limit he states is raw AoE, where Havoc is clearly behind Devourer (about 700k at eight targets against Devourer's 700k at five), so the case for Havoc rests on priority damage and funnel rather than pack throughput.

takes.creator: J-Funk
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — dedicated "should you play Windwalker in 12.1" spec overview, recorded 2026-08-04
takes.claim: He calls Windwalker a bit of an underdog going into the new raid: in testing it was fine on most fights but not exceptional, because the spec received very little until a late undocumented hotfix pass buffed Spinning Crane Kick by roughly 40%. That buff made two-target damage substantial, which is where he expects the payoff — Windwalker will not shine on the early spread-cleave fights but gains real value on the later two-target encounters, and he describes it as flat-out overpowered on Twin Fangs, where the adds die very quickly and the two-boss damage is also good. Coiled Altar is named as the other beneficiary. He is explicit that Ula'tek itself is an unknown, but concludes Windwalker looks a pretty decent option for raid this season. Build-wise, early sims put Conduit slightly ahead of Shadopan with both close; Conduit keeps more burst and more synergy with the Season 2 tier set, which he rates a major step up from Season 1 and impactful enough to change AoE muscle memory. He records the caveat himself: this is an August 4th read and a hotfix nerf could undo it.

takes.creator: J-Funk
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — dedicated "should you play Windwalker in 12.1" spec overview, recorded 2026-08-04
takes.claim: His M+ read is markedly stronger than his raid read. He notes Windwalker has not been relevant in M+ for five years — its last meta season was Shadowlands Season 3 — and says that after extensive testing following the latest buffs he is thrilled to report the spec might be on the precipice of another meta season. The case rests on AoE: he believes Windwalker may have some of the highest AoE burst in the game and that its sustained AoE is decent too, with Spinning Crane Kick doing most of the heavy lifting after its buff. Survivability has improved slightly, helped by a defensive node in the tree and by spending less time in melee. He states the weakness plainly — single-target damage is a little suspect — but says it can be played around by dragging adds onto the boss. He also expects the utility to matter this season, singling out the number of physical-damage nukes that can be cheesed with Dance of the Wind, and predicts Windwalker will be pretty popular in M+. Same self-imposed caveat: recorded August 4th, and hotfix nerfs could reverse it.

takes.creator: Musguete
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — review of PTR M+ logs across all three Rogue specs after the Rogue buff pass
takes.claim: Reviewing PTR M+ logs after the Rogue buffs, he puts Outlaw well ahead of where it sat the previous week and well ahead of Subtlety, citing a first page of logs already reaching almost 550k overall and 424k / 414k on Ruby Life Pools, and comparing favourably against Shadow Priest and Demon Hunter parses on the same keys. He says that if Blizzard wants Rogue at that level, Outlaw will be S tier in a physical comp. The honest limit he keeps returning to is not the damage but the delivery: Outlaw remains heavily dependent on the Roll the Bones jackpot, damage can drop off a lot without it, and he expects that RNG dependence to put players off even while the numbers are strong — he says he wants damage to depend on rotation rather than luck. He is explicit that he expects a nerf soon precisely because the numbers are this high. He also flags a methodology caveat on his own evidence twice: Warcraft Logs itself warns that treating testing data as live data is incorrect and inaccurate, and he stresses that pull count drives these overall numbers, walking through dungeons cleared in 7, 11 and 15 pulls to show why the same key level produces very different overalls.

takes.creator: Musguete
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — review of PTR M+ logs across all three Rogue specs after the Rogue buff pass
takes.claim: He identifies Assassination as the spec that got the most out of the buff pass — he puts the total at roughly 16% increased overall damage — and reads it as the best-performing Rogue spec overall. He shows more than a million damage on the burst window and says the sustain afterwards is what impresses him more, continuing to ramp after the burst and holding up even without Death Mark, on King's Bane alone. Logs cited: 443k overall on Altar of Fangs, and two parses above 300k on Murder Row, which he singles out because no Rogue spec had previously exceeded 300k there. He notes the build shown takes four nodes in the Apex talent, i.e. the far Apex route Blizzard intends players to use. He stops short of calling it the best spec of Season 2 — he says it is still too early with two weeks to launch and expects changes through the first two weeks of the raid — but says Assassination currently feels the best to play of the three and, like Outlaw, that he expects it to be the most nerfed if Blizzard does not want Rogue at this level. King's Rest is called out as awful for every Rogue spec.

takes.creator: Obli
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Blood DK discussion with a guest; the DPS-DK consequence is Obli's own read
takes.claim: The video is about Blood, but Obli — whose authority here is the DPS specs — draws an explicit consequence for them. Because Blood brings no raid buff, its only real utility is Death Grip, and in a group that already has a Blood DK a Frost DK loses a lot of its value: he says that in a lot of groups Blood being brought alienates the other DKs precisely through grip redundancy. He goes further and says that in M+ it does not matter how good Frost looks, because Blood is simultaneously so offensively and so defensively strong that it is difficult to place a DPS DK at all when Blood is doing this well. He notes Blood is expected to be nerfed for raid overperformance and that such a nerf would land unintentionally on keys too, but his DPS-DK point is about roster displacement rather than tuning. Separately, on the raid side he says that in a Race to World First context he cannot see DPS DKs really being brought — one at most — given Blood's single-target and defensive profile; that is a world-first roster observation rather than a general raid read.

takes.creator: Obli
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Blood DK discussion with a guest; the DPS-DK consequence is Obli's own read
takes.claim: Same read as for Frost, stated by Obli in the same breath. Blood DK brings no raid buff and its only real utility is Death Grip, so an Unholy DK in a group that already fields a Blood DK loses a lot of its value to grip redundancy — he says bringing Blood alienates the other DKs. He then says that in M+ it does not matter how good Unholy looks, because Blood is strong enough on both offence and defence that placing a DPS DK becomes hard when Blood is performing this well. He expects Blood to be nerfed for raid overperformance with keys caught in the blast, but the point about Unholy is displacement rather than tuning. On the raid side he adds that in a Race to World First he cannot see DPS DKs being brought beyond one at most — a world-first roster observation, not a general raid verdict.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — PTR M+ and raid healer testing stream; explicit upward revision of his own tier list
takes.claim: He states plainly that he thinks Restoration Shaman will be strong in raid and that he underrated it in his own latest tier list. The reason he gives is a class talent he says he had overlooked: Elemental Resistance, which makes Healing Stream Totem's healing also reduce Fire, Frost and Nature damage taken by 6%. Because so much of Restoration Shaman's healing comes through totems the effect is close to permanently applied, and because the incoming raid is almost entirely Nature damage he describes it as effectively a Devotion Aura for Resto Shamans — roughly as much mitigation as Devotion grants, stacked on top of the Skyfury/vigor stamina the spec already brings. His conclusion is that Resto Shaman is going to be real good in the new raid and that his published tier list placement was too low.

takes.creator: Megasett
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his own Dummy Dome healer-dummy testing under vendor gear, no over-tuned trinkets/embellishments by agreement
takes.claim: He reports Mistweaver doing roughly 40% less healing than the strongest healers on the PTR healer dummy and calls it an insane fall-off from an excellent Season 1. He attributes it to a stack of losses rather than one change: a 3% aura nerf one week and a 7% aura nerf the next, a 60% cut to Morning Breeze that left the mastery rework not paying off, and the loss of the Season 1 four-piece he estimates at about 15% of the spec's HPS. He tested three builds — high-mastery Chi-Ji, normal-stat Chi-Ji and Yulon — and got essentially the same numbers from all of them, with Chi-Ji collapsing into fishing for Rising Sun Kick resets because Renewing Mist, Vivify and Enveloping Mist were all HPS losses; he notes the dummy gave 100% melee uptime that the Venomous Abyss bosses will not. He is harshest on the cooldowns: Revival does about 675,000 total healing on a three-minute cooldown and is outhealed by class-tree passives, Yulon does not feel like a cooldown at all, and Celestial Conduit contributes under 3% of healing. Because Mistweaver brings little beyond throughput, he argues it needs to be among the highest healers to justify a slot, and his conclusion is that he will not bring it to the raid — he plans Restoration Shaman and Holy Paladin instead, with the Monk as a late farm character. He frames it as a tuning problem rather than the bugs that held the spec back in early Midnight, and notes there is no heroic week this time to absorb it.

takes.creator: Megasett
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Mythic+ aside in his Dummy Dome raid-testing review
takes.claim: Separating keys from raid, he is markedly less negative: he says he will still have his Mistweaver for keys and reads it as pretty mid-pack there rather than unplayable, adding that a mid-pack placement has not stopped him playing it before. He gives no supporting numbers for the Mythic+ read — his testing was the raid healer dummy — so it stands as a plain placement call alongside the detailed raid case.

takes.creator: Musguete
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR (2026-07-31 build) — reaction to the rogue aura buffs in that day's class tuning
takes.claim: Reading the 2026-07-31 rogue tuning, he reports Outlaw receiving a 6% all-damage increase (PvP excluded) alongside Assassination's 10% and Subtlety's 10%, and reads the pass as clearly positive — his words are that things are looking much better for rogues now and that Blizzard is finally hearing the community. He credits Zartar's analysis video with driving the change. He gives no placement or comparison against other classes and says he still has to see how it performs on the PTR, so this is a read on the direction of the tuning rather than on where Outlaw lands.

takes.creator: Musguete
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR (2026-07-31 build) — reaction to the rogue aura buffs in that day's class tuning
takes.claim: He singles out Assassination's 10% damage buff as the headline of the 2026-07-31 rogue tuning and says it is very good and needed — the spec wanted damage and got it. As with his Outlaw read he stops short of a placement call, saying he will test on the PTR and report back, so the claim is about the direction of the change rather than the resulting standing.

takes.creator: Bansherz
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 key testing stream; answering directly on where Hunter lands in keys
takes.claim: Asked to rank Marksmanship, he puts it at roughly B tier and says he would place all three Hunter specs around B. His framing is that Hunter is solid and in a pretty good spot but simply not meta — his advice is that a Hunter main or one-trick will be completely fine, while someone chasing the best spec in the game should not swap to Hunter. He also says that with no Hunter spec overtuned the right approach is to flex between at least the two ranged specs rather than commit to one, and he confirms he is staying on Hunter himself. He caveats that a buff could land any day and change the placement.

takes.creator: Bansherz
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 key testing stream; answering directly on where Hunter lands in keys
takes.claim: He groups Beast Mastery with the rest of the class at around B tier for keys — solid, in a pretty good spot, but not meta. The same advice follows: fine for a Hunter main, not the pick for someone chasing the strongest spec, and worth flexing between the ranged specs rather than committing. He flags that tuning could still move it.

takes.creator: Bansherz
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 key testing stream; answering directly on where Hunter lands in keys
takes.claim: Within a class he places around B tier for keys, he singles out Survival as probably the highest of the three — higher B tier — while keeping it inside the same 'solid but not meta' band as Marksmanship and Beast Mastery. He adds the same caveat that Hunter could be buffed at any point before launch.

takes.creator: Bansherz
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 Survival Hunter guide (tier set + build read; complements, not replaces, his 08-07 M+ tier placement)
takes.claim: He rates the Season 2 two-piece highly: Mongoose Fury now also amplifies the bomb for roughly 10% more damage, which he calls very big and strong in both single target and AoE, and wants equipped as soon as possible. The four-piece he reads as slightly weaker in single target and good in AoE, extending Mongoose Fury while channelling Boomstick. He also expects Sentinel to be the build in both raid and keys rather than the Pack Leader build played on live, and says haste gains value this season while crit loses some, because bombs recharge with haste.

takes.creator: Tactyks
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — asked on stream which tanks the Season 2 raid comp wants, at current tuning
takes.claim: Asked directly what the 12.1 raid tank comp might look like, he answers that at current tuning it is definitely still Protection Paladin, and that Prot Paladin is looking very good. He frames the rest of the raid tank picture as largely unchanged from Season 1 to Season 2 apart from that Protection Paladin shift, and separately calls Protection Warrior still a brick wall.

takes.creator: Tactyks
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — tank testing in Season 2 keys, after that build's Protection Paladin nerfs
takes.claim: Tanking Season 2 keys on the PTR after the recent nerfs, he says Protection Paladin still seems fine and is still definitely looking like the best tank. He notes the nerfs landed slightly lighter than he expected and hit somewhat different parts of the kit than he had predicted.

takes.creator: Jedith
takes.claim: He reads the pass as a partial walk-back rather than a real gain: all damage up 5%, but that only restores the previous build's across-the-board nerf, with Immolation Aura's damage and Fury generation cut and moved into active abilities and Demon Blades. Essence Break's initial hit is up 35% and should give good burst. His overall verdict is still negative — Havoc remains pretty low on DPS compared with the rest of the field — and he flags that the Venomous Abyss four-piece is bugged, buffing the Chaos Strike / Blade Dance proc inside the window rather than Essence Break's initial hit as the tooltip says.

takes.creator: Jedith
takes.claim: On the tuning itself he is unimpressed — Collapsing Star up 12% is not enough to make it worth pressing outside the Apex-talent builds, and Eradicate is down 6% — but his standing read on the spec is positive: he places Devourer up there, says it feels pretty good after the previous build's aura buff, and expects the Void Scourge melee-combo build to be the one played into the patch, with Annihilator still viable and some players doing very good damage on it.

takes.creator: NeekapHere
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Divine Storm buff plus his own Season 2 key testing
takes.claim: He welcomes Divine Storm's 10% buff as small but needed and most useful in AoE, then reports that Retribution did not feel the best in his PTR keys — his abilities, particularly Final Verdict and Divine Storm on Herald, did not feel like they were doing anything, though he caveats that his groups and pull sizes were poor. He reads single target as feeling pretty good with the tier set changes and AoE as the weak side, rates Templar ahead of Herald in both, and says Herald is not fun in M+ because the tier set adds yet another button to a build that already has more globals' worth of priority abilities than it can press.

takes.creator: leak
takes.claim: He calls reverting Hunter's Mark to a single target a really bad change. In raid it means a guild wants two hunters on the several two- and three-target Venomous Abyss encounters purely to mark them, which he argues is backwards for a raid buff. In M+ he reads single-target Hunter's Mark as one of the worst raid buffs in the game — worth roughly 0.7% over a key run against something like Mark of the Wild — and concludes Hunters will not be brought to keys unless their own damage is exceptional.

takes.creator: leak
takes.claim: He reads the hero-tree picture as settled by bug fixes rather than tuning: the Pack Leader boar was benefiting from mastery twice and losing that is roughly a 3-4% damage cut, which he considers large and uncompensated, and which pushes Sentinel clearly ahead of Pack Leader for all content after the two were close in sims. He likes the Grenade Juggler redesign (Boomstick giving 60% bomb cooldown recovery) but says it still is not strong enough to run over the competing talents in either single target or AoE, and that the Open Fire rework does not beat Stargazer.

takes.creator: Sam
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 Frost DK build and tier-set read for keys
takes.claim: He reads the Season 2 tier set as built around Icy Talons and therefore as pushing Frost into dual wield, since the effect keys off auto-attack critical strikes and is stronger with two weapons; he says two-handed is not in a good spot with this tier set. For keys he recommends Rune of Razorice main hand with Rune of the Fallen Crusader off hand, and notes the easier Breath of Sindragosa build (dropping Frostbane) is what most players are running on the PTR and is competitive with the alternative, with Remorseless Winter and Icy Touch Torrent the top abilities.

takes.creator: Tactyks
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Venomous Abyss raid-testing preview (superseded by his 07-21 raid-comp read)
takes.claim: From mythic testing of Twin Fangs he reports the guild bringing four Protection Paladins to trivialise the roughly twelve-snake interrupt mechanic, but expects the live answer to be assignments rather than stacking — one Protection Paladin very useful, not required. He also notes tanks with magic immunities (Blood DK Anti-Magic Shell, Paladin bubble or Spell Warding) could cheese part of the Coven tank soak for massively reduced raid damage, and expects Blizzard to make that dot pierce immunities before launch.

takes.creator: Musguete
takes.claim: He reads the pass as a solid win for Assassination: all damage up 6%, rank three Impeccable Strike up 15%, and the Venomous Abyss four-piece now giving 3% melee damage per Amplifying Poison stack instead of 2%. He adds that before these changes Assassination was performing a little worse than Outlaw but ahead of Subtlety.

takes.creator: Musguete
takes.claim: For Outlaw he reads the pass as very good: overall damage up 3% and Audacity increasing Ambush damage by 80% instead of 60%. He frames the whole build as Blizzard finally responding to rogue community feedback across all three specs.

takes.creator: Musguete
takes.claim: He reads the Killing Spree rework as a real buff and a rotation change: combo points spent beyond maximum now add 15% damage instead of extending the duration, and Adrenaline Rush speeds Killing Spree's execution by 20%, so the opener becomes Adrenaline Rush into Killing Spree rather than Between the Eyes. He is disappointed the same build left Subtlety's earlier 8% nerf uncompensated.

takes.creator: Obli
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — June build shifting Frost damage out of burst
takes.claim: He reads the build as the change he had been asking for: Howling Blast damage doubled, with Obliterate, Frost Fever, Remorseless Winter and Frost Strike also up, against a Pillar of Frost nerf that Enduring Strength largely offsets and a 30% Frostbane cut that nets to roughly 10% after the Deathly Blows increase. His verdict is that Frost still does pretty good but is not quite as good as Unholy, which he attributes largely to a strong trinket. He measures dual wield about 10% ahead of two-handed on his own logs and expects Icy Death Rune in every build.

takes.creator: Kesslive
takes.claim: He reads the Wingleader redesign as gutting Augmentation rather than tuning it: cooldown reduction now comes only from Mass Disintegrate and Mass Eruption, which he and the Evoker Discord's feedback post put at roughly a 65% AoE and 75-80% single-target cooldown loss, leaving one duplicate instead of the triple and quadruple duplicates the spec's competitive damage depended on. He calls the 40% Commander's Squadron and maneuverability compensation far too small, says it forces full-length Breath of Eons flights he considers unfun and risky, and endorses the conclusion that competitive damage is impossible as it stands.

takes.creator: Kesslive
takes.claim: He reads Devastation as collateral damage in a change aimed at Augmentation — hit because it shares the Scale Commander hero tree — and says the lost cooldown reduction compounds an essence economy that already leans heavily on Imminent Destruction. He also doubts the common suggestion to swap to Chrono Warden, betting Chrono Warden still trails Scale Commander for M+ damage.

takes.creator: Megasett
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 mastery build for keys
takes.claim: After a second 50% mastery buff (roughly 100% across the 12.1 tuning so far) he reports key builds stacking upwards of 1,300 mastery, because mastery scales Rising Sun Kick's damage and therefore its Ancient Teachings healing, making it the highest-priority button at any target count. He rates it good numerically for both healing and damage and more fun than Spinning Crane Kick spam, and says it further sinks Master of Harmony behind the conduit tree — but he expects it not to go live this strong, dislikes so much throughput sitting on one button, and warns the build leaves almost no healing outside melee.

takes.creator: Sha
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — week-six tank changes; Brewmaster received none
takes.claim: In a build that buffed most tanks he notes Brewmaster and Guardian Druid received nothing. He says monk is down bad and that he keeps calling it dead without quite meaning it — it is still a fine tank that performs okay, does decent single target on Master of Harmony, and brings Tiger's Lust and Detox — but the class feels worse to play, citing an undocumented Celestial Infusion change that Blizzard never put in any notes, a small concentration effect to stand in, and a rotation that can stop flowing when the Apex talent does not reset.

takes.creator: Sha
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — controlled same-gear tank damage/survivability comparison in keys
takes.claim: From a controlled large-pull comparison he places both Brewmaster builds in the middle group at roughly 410-450k, behind Annihilator DH and the two DK trees. His main concern is the tier set: it is coded to only a handful of physical abilities so Flurry Strikes largely misses it, and the flame-patch damage that read as 10% of his output in a stand-still test is cut about in half or worse in real keys where he kites and chains pulls, which he calls really disappointing. The positive side is Vital Flame healing restored to 50% and benefiting from the tier set, which he says is why Brewmaster survived the large pulls.

takes.creator: leak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — bomb-build changes (superseded by his 07-24 read)
takes.claim: He reads the bomb changes as putting Sentinel genuinely in play: it feels great because of the extra cooldown reduction and may end up better than Pack Leader, with Mongoose Rounds plus Boomstick giving a strong mini cooldown. He says he would love to play Sentinel for a tier after four seasons of Pack Leader, while doubting a flat damage buff would make Open Fire competitive with Stargazer.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Oracle Holy Priest key testing
takes.claim: Testing Oracle Holy Priest in Season 2 keys he says the spec can do a ton of healing and singles out Lightweaver with Prayer of Mending as really strong, while framing the open question as whether raw healing output is what has been holding Holy Priest back in dungeons or whether the spec needs a broader look. He tempers the read by noting the group is coming out of a very strong season for healers.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 Holy Paladin M+ testing
takes.claim: After testing the build he calls Holy Paladin really really strong and probably one of the best healers right now, specifically one of the best in M+, crediting the build and the tier set and the flexibility to swap between spot healing and AoE healing through Virtues. His reservation is a design one — he still wants to press Holy Shock to heal rather than for damage — and he is unsure what Blizzard will do with it.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 healer re-test, Holy Paladin vs Holy Priest
takes.claim: Re-testing the healers against each other he lands on Holy Paladin as the best healer, saying surprisingly it is probably the best right now — while immediately adding that he expects it to get changed before the patch ships.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.claim: He opens by calling Mistweaver meta again and OP again, reporting that the Spinning Crane Kick build survived the tuning — a Windwalker talent that had bled into its power was fixed, but Blizzard then buffed Spinning Crane Kick in the latest build. He separately questions whether the Apex talents make sense for Mistweaver in keys, since they largely go unused there.

takes.creator: Pkpawner
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 Windwalker build and boss testing
takes.claim: He deliberately assesses the spec's damage profile rather than its current numbers, on the grounds that tuning moves week to week. His read is that the encounters expose a structural weakness: two-target cleave is already not great for Windwalker and several tested fights alternate between two-target and pure single target, with one mob that cannot be stacked and another that teleports. He found Conduit good on some bosses and really bad on that one, and read the fight as Shado-Pan coded.

takes.creator: Tettles
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his final pre-launch Season 2 Mythic+ DPS tier list
takes.claim: He places Moonkin among his 'really good comp filler' group rather than the A+ meta core, reading it as quite good at boss damage in keys but somewhat behind on overall damage. His argument for it is Mark of the Wild, which he counts with Skyfury as one of the two premium raid buffs, and he notes no season since the 0.1% title existed has gone without a Druid in the meta groups — but he explicitly leaves open whether that holds this time.

takes.creator: Tettles
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his final pre-launch Season 2 Mythic+ DPS tier list
takes.claim: He drops the spec to C tier, below the B-tier group. His stated reason is the Wing Leader nerf, which he says stopped Augmentation from keeping double duplicates out, and he judges that nothing since has buffed it nearly enough to compensate.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — final pre-launch Season 2 Mythic+ spec tier list update
takes.claim: He keeps Blood in S+ and reads it as both the tankiest tank and the highest-damage one, explicitly noting the placement survives the most recent nerf. He later describes tanking as an island — every other tank sits a tier lower missing either damage or survivability — and builds all three of his suggested meta comps around Blood.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — final pre-launch Season 2 Mythic+ spec tier list update
takes.claim: He keeps Holy Paladin in S+ as the best healer at keeping a group alive. He names two real costs — weak healer damage and no raid buff — but resolves them in the spec's favour on the grounds that survival is what a healer is for. He stays unconvinced by the Preservation Evoker case that is pulling other people's lists, saying he wants to see it heal high keys consistently first.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — final pre-launch Season 2 Mythic+ spec tier list update
takes.claim: He calls Arms probably the best DPS in the game right now, or at least the best melee, and keeps it in S+. His reasons are the combination he considers decisive for this season: good funnel, good priority damage and good target swapping, plus a lot of AoE and stops, on a spec that can make itself tanky with Spell Reflection and Defensive Stance when needed.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — final pre-launch Season 2 Mythic+ spec tier list update
takes.claim: Of the non-Blood tanks he says Protection Warrior is missing the most, and his reasoning is that it has been conditional since Dragonflight: it is only good where Spell Reflection is good. He gives Ruby Life Pools as the dungeon where that pays off and says it is completely useless in some others, landing it at the bottom of his A- tank group.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — final pre-launch Season 2 Mythic+ spec tier list update
takes.claim: He puts every Druid spec in A and says they are not good enough that he would bring one even after counting Mark of the Wild and Stampeding Roar. On Guardian specifically he reads it as tanky enough but short on damage if built for survivability. He adds the flip side: because the buff floor for a Mark of the Wild carrier is lower, one buff to Guardian or one nerf to Blood would put it back into his fizz comp.

takes.creator: YoDaTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — final pre-launch Season 2 Mythic+ spec tier list update
takes.claim: He drops Retribution to B and reads it as significantly worse than last season, naming a few bosses that make it bad to play. His comparative point is that it competes for the same non-buff-carrying damage slot as the Rogue specs, and he considers Rogue far better this season.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his published 12.1 Demonology guide, closing assessment
takes.claim: Closing his 12.1 guide he says not much really changed for Demonology relative to 12.0 and that it feels like the spec is doing less damage, which he attributes to tuning rather than design and expects may be buffed over the following weeks. On builds he reads Soul Harvester as simming higher in pure single target but expects Diabolist to be what is actually played, since the tier has only one true patchwerk fight and Diabolist carries the stacked cleave profile.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 main/alt plan, raid spec choice
takes.claim: Explaining why he expects to raid as Discipline again rather than Holy, he says Holy Priest still looks really undertuned for the raid at the moment. He frames it as the same call he made in Season 1, where he tried Holy on a couple of fights, found it decidedly worse, and played 90% of the tier as Discipline.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 main/alt plan, raid spec choice
takes.claim: He reads Discipline as being in a very powerful position for the Season 2 raid and expects to main it for his guild rather than Holy. In his separate PTR raid-testing tier list the same day he keeps it in S tier, where his stated criterion for S is stackability — he argues stacking two Discipline is better than stacking two Preservation because the damage advantage is sizable, while flagging a high chance the double-Discipline setup gets nerfed.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 Mythic+ healer testing stream (Dummy Dome / key testing)
takes.claim: Playing Holy in keys he reads the dungeon side as clearly improved — healing feels a lot better than the Season 1 version he says was very hard to push rating on, and mana in dungeons is a lot better too, though he notes it stays a problem in raid. The offsetting weakness is survivability, which he calls still really bad: he finds himself spending a lot of extra globals healing himself compared with other healers.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 main/alt plan, alt spec choice
takes.claim: He describes Mistweaver as bouncing all over the place through the PTR tuning passes and does not commit to its current standing, but expects it to land in a very strong position by the season, on the grounds that its developer seems more locked in than most. He is bringing it as one of two alts for split runs.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 main/alt plan, alt spec choice
takes.claim: He reads Holy Paladin as being in a good place for Season 2 and gives a mechanism rather than just the usual 'it does a lot of healing' line: the 30% increases to player health pools and creature damage make Holy Light a more efficient cast, where in Season 1 the spec was overweight on Holy Light spam that cost enormous mana and overhealed. He adds that the Season 2 tier set amplifies this by guaranteeing Infusion of Light procs, and is taking it as an alt.

takes.creator: Preheat
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Mage roundtable (Porom, Forgy, Khaelt, Azuna), Season 2 raid outlook
takes.claim: Hosting a 12.1 Mage roundtable with the class's theorycrafters, Preheat and the panel land on Sunfury Arcane as the default Mage raid spec for Season 2: asked which spec is the de facto pick, every participant leans Arcane for most of the raid, with Preheat saying that if he had to choose one spec for the whole tier he would play Arcane and expects to take it on every boss that matters. The reasons given are defensive rather than throughput — the new Prismatic Barrier window plus refractive Mirror Image give Arcane by far the strongest defensive kit of the three specs, which matters most in early progression — plus the removal of Arcane's mana constraint and strong 3-5 target damage on top of its single-target missiles.

takes.creator: Preheat
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Mage roundtable (Porom, Forgy, Khaelt, Azuna), Season 2 raid outlook
takes.claim: The panel reads 12.1 as taking Frost's defining niche away: Splitting Ice and Fractured Frost cuts gut the two-target cleave that had been roughly doubling its damage on PTR, and the Glacial Spike cleave no longer smart-targets the way Ice Lance did, so the loss lands hardest on spread two-target. Their conclusion for the raid is that Frost drops to a situational pick on the genuinely stacked two-target bosses (the turtles, the snakes) while Arcane takes the rest, and that Frost is now clearly weaker than Arcane on defensives in a material way. Beyond the two-target nerf they describe the spec as largely untouched across the PTR cycle — a new tier set and little else.

takes.creator: Preheat
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Mage roundtable (Porom, Forgy, Khaelt, Azuna), Season 2 M+ outlook
takes.claim: On keys the panel says 12.1 leaves Frost's long-standing uncapped-AoE hole unaddressed — Blizzard and Frozen Orb still contribute little, so a Spellslinger Frost can be out-damaged by a tank on a dungeon's first pull — and no talent rework around Blizzard arrived. What did improve is feel rather than output: the Season 2 set pushes Frostfire, and the more frequent procs make the icicle/Glacial Spike gameplay noticeably more reactive.

takes.creator: Preheat
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Mage roundtable (Porom, Forgy, Khaelt, Azuna), Season 2 outlook
takes.claim: The panel's read on Fire is that 12.1 gave it numbers instead of attention: a second Blazing Barrier charge plus flat aura percentages, while Arcane and Frost received real defensive tools (Arcane's Prismatic Barrier window, Frost's short Ice Cold) and Fire's defensive budget stays locked in Cauterize, which the player never controls. They also dislike the Season 2 set steering Fire onto Pyroclasm, a talent nobody has played. Nobody on the panel expects Fire to be competitive at the start of Season 2 — Preheat signs off saying 'make Fire great again, but not this tier', and plans to play Sunfury Arcane.

takes.creator: Bansherz
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 Beast Mastery guide (talent, tier-set and hero-tree read; complements, not replaces, his 08-07 M+ tier placement)
takes.claim: In his Season 2 Beast Mastery guide he reads the 12.1 changes as a net gain. Beast Cleave going to a 10-second duration against an unchanged 8-second Wild Thrash cooldown gives 100% Beast Cleave uptime without holding globals, which he calls a massive quality-of-life change, and Beast Cleave's own damage is up; Kill Command is buffed while Kill Cleave is nerfed, which he reads as trading a little AoE for more single target. On the tier set, the two-piece adds a second pet stomp at 50% effectiveness and the four-piece makes stomp empower the next Cobra Shot, giving Cobra Shot a real rotational role rather than being pure filler. His clearest structural call is that Dark Ranger has little reason to be played next season in either bracket: the tier set rewards Cobra Shot, which Pack Leader spams as its only filler while Dark Ranger splits its filler between Cobra Shot and Black Arrow, and he reads the talent changes as favouring Pack Leader too — so he expects to play Pack Leader in both raid and keys, keeping Dark Ranger only where its defensives are needed. He also splits stat priorities by bracket: mastery then crit with very low haste in keys, mastery then roughly even crit and haste in raid, and effectively zero versatility in both.

takes.creator: Tactyks
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his Season 2 tank rankings and tier list, raid section (supersedes his 07-21 raid-comp read)
takes.claim: Two days before launch he reads Protection Paladin as one of the stronger raid tanks after the PTR reworks: really solid, noticeably tankier than Season 1, with output he rates as pretty good, and he places it high in his raid tier — discussed immediately below Blood Death Knight, which he puts on top. The tempering factor is roster composition rather than the spec's own power: Holy Paladin is looking strong and a group already bringing one may not want a second Paladin buff, though he notes Holy Paladin looks stronger in M+ than in raid. Even then he sees a real case for Protection Paladin on immunity and Spell Warding shenanigans that are unique to the spec, and singles out Twin Fangs as a fight with obvious Prot Paladin interactions via both the immunities and Avenger's Shield interrupts. His conclusion is explicitly two-sided: he would not be surprised if one of the two raid tanks were a Protection Paladin, and equally would not be surprised if there were none, because of Holy Paladin's perceived dominance.

takes.creator: Tactyks
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his Season 2 tank rankings and tier list, Mythic+ section
takes.claim: In keys he places Protection Paladin just below the top tanks — a decent spot, not the best but a little below that — after a PTR arc in which two talent-tree reworks left it briefly overtuned and then trimmed back over subsequent weeks. He characterises the net change as less power in Wings and more in the baseline: a flat 10% damage reduction on Blessed Hammer, Word of Glory able to overheal into a shield, and access to both crit Wings and Sentinel, against a shorter Wings duration that lowers uptime noticeably at launch until stats catch up, plus a toned-down Apex node. He reads the spec as net more defensive than in Season 1, which he calls its major Season 1 weakness. His caveat is again composition: Holy Paladin is strong enough that groups are unlikely to run two Paladins, which can cost Protection Paladin a slot, though it regains value alongside a non-Paladin healer. He notes several tuning passes are still to come.

takes.creator: Nintern
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 Devourer guide, recorded with the double-haste bug still live
takes.claim: He opens his Season 2 guide by stating Devourer is "really strong on PTR right now" and that there is a chance it simply gets flattened or nerfed, because a bug currently lets several Devourer abilities — he names Consume and Cull — benefit twice from haste while in Void Meta, which he says spikes the spec "quite a bit" in sims and in real gameplay alike. He judges the build recommendations unlikely to change regardless: Void-Scarred melee for all content, with Annihilator fine in M+ but carried by the spec's overall strength rather than its own, which he calls "kind of a pad spec" against Void-Scarred's cleave and priority damage.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ outlook (healer prep stream)
takes.claim: His strongest Holy Paladin read yet: he calls it a blaster for next season and, unusually, argues it is not cooldown-reliant — he rates Wings as unimpressive and says the spec simply does consistently insane healing through Holy Light, Virtues and consumed Infusions, with very strong spot healing that converts into Virtue AoE healing. He also stresses accessibility, repeatedly saying it is easy to play while looking really strong, and lists it among the three healers he intends to main. His caveat is hoping it does not get nerfed before launch.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ outlook (healer prep stream)
takes.claim: He recommends it as the easy-and-good healer and explains the mechanism: totems give constant "buffer" healing so a slow or imprecise player is punished far less than on healers where every heal is a discrete press. He names it his main for the season. The M+ caveat he is explicit about is that its tier set wants the group stacked — with two ranged in a pug who will not stack, he says the tier set is partly wasted and far-field play drives you nuts.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ outlook (healer prep stream)
takes.claim: A clear step down from his early-August read. He calls it chill and easy to pick up but says plainly he does not think it will be perceived as good next season. His specific complaints are mobility and button availability: no Renew, Shadow Word: Pain replaced on the talent, so the only things to press while moving are Chastise, Serenity and Holy Word cooldowns, none of them spammable — something he says took him a while to adjust to.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ outlook (healer prep stream)
takes.claim: A more balanced read than his late-July write-off. He reports Mistweaver actually has decent numbers, can put out reasonable damage while still healing enough for high keys, and that the new talent makes the Apex build work better. But he identifies the core problem as Vivify and Sheilun’s Gift being very weak, which he calls the biggest issue with the spec on the Season 2 PTR, and says he is near-certain it is getting buffs while pointing out none have arrived yet.

takes.creator: Nintern
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 Havoc guide (talents, tier set, stats, trinkets, rotation; raid and M+)
takes.claim: His read is continuity rather than a power swing: the builds are largely unchanged and he describes nothing earth-shattering in the rotation. The concrete 12.1 changes he names are that Inertia was nerfed on the PTR to 12%, so Exergy is now the pick and the rotation gets simpler, and that the Season 1 tier set’s 6% haste is gone, so gearing leans slightly more into haste while the priority stays crit > mastery > haste > versatility. On the Season 2 set — 2-piece giving Blade Dance, Chaos Strike and Essence Break +12%, 4-piece making Essence Break benefit from Cycle of Hatred with +35% initial strike damage and +2s duration — he is explicit that it is not a huge damage gain, contrasting it directly with Devourer’s, which he puts at around 25%. Every Havoc build takes Essence Break because of it, and it is strong enough to be used on cooldown rather than held to line up. On hero talents: Aldrachi Reaver runs one build for everything, which he counts an advantage, but is lower raw AoE than Fel-Scarred — so raid is generally Aldrachi Reaver throughout, while M+ is Fel-Scarred unless the comp specifically needs its funnel and physical damage.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his published Season 2 Warlock guide site (hero-talent picks per bracket + Venomous Abyss per-boss spec recommendations)
takes.claim: Build guidance rather than a power verdict, and current as of the same day. For raid he reports a mix of Hellcaller and Diabolist actually being played; for M+ he calls Hellcaller the better option, framing the choice as Hellcaller’s tremendous AoE against Diabolist’s strong priority damage with solid passive AoE. In his Season 2 Venomous Abyss guide Destruction is the recommended spec on five of the seven bosses he has called — the Entombed Sentinels, the Lost Explorers, Sszorak, the Twin Fangs and the Coiled Altar — with Ula’tek still TBD. Worth reading as an intra-Warlock recommendation about which of the three to bring per fight, not as a claim about Destruction’s standing against other classes.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his published Season 2 Warlock guide site, M+ section
takes.claim: The one genuine comparative on the site, and it is scoped to M+: he calls Demonology the most consistent of the three Warlock specs in keys, built on a strong cleave profile with Demonic Tyrant on a short one-minute cooldown, and says that while it may not be as strong at the high end it is arguably the better pick in lower and mid-tier keys. Diabolist is his hero talent for M+. This is a relative read about which Warlock to bring to a key and does not revise his separate, blunter assessment that the spec is undertuned.

takes.creator: Kalamazi
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his published Season 2 Warlock guide site (hero-talent picks per bracket + Venomous Abyss per-boss spec recommendations)
takes.claim: Build guidance, with no power claim attached. Soul Harvester is his pick in both raid and M+, and he explains the M+ trade-off as Soul Harvester’s more upfront burst and stronger single target against Hellcaller’s strong AoE through Wither and Malevolence. In the Season 2 Venomous Abyss guide Affliction shares the recommendation with Demonology on Nek’zali the Soulcoiler and Vashnik the Malignant. Note this sits alongside, and does not revise, his far blunter sims-based reads of the spec’s raw power.

takes.creator: Ellesmere
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 quickview build guide (wingsisup.com), replacing his 12.0.5 one
takes.claim: His Season 2 quickview rebuilds Holy Paladin around the tier set: Infusion of Light on Flash of Light inside Virtue windows is what drives the playstyle, with a ~25% haste baseline taken first and then Versatility for high keys, Mastery for raw healing and Crit as filler. Two 12.1 kit observations sit under the build advice — Aura Mastery now also casts Divine Toll, which he says finally makes it a real healing cooldown in M+, and Wings wants holding more reserved than in previous seasons because the spec has less cooldown power overall. He makes no comparative claim about where Holy Paladin stands against other healers, and the raid section is self-labelled the pre-patch build; the page's only aside on standing is that his full guide stays shelved unless Hpal "becomes meta".

takes.creator: Harrek
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his analysis of the healer Dummy Dome testing session (a raid-style five-minute damage ramp)
takes.claim: From the 12.1 PTR healer Dummy Dome session — a full raid of high-level healers on a dummy that ramps damage over five minutes — he reads Restoration Shaman as gaining substantially in Season 2, with haste as the change that matters: Riptide's heal-over-time is doubled and extendable through the new Swelling Tides, Healing Rain is buffed, the tier set randomly spawns extra Healing Rains (more of them the more haste you carry) and the 4-piece shields on every Healing Rain tick rather than the tooltip's stated one second, while the higher crit reachable in Season 2 feeds Resurgence and eases the mana ceiling that made haste unattractive in Season 1. He settles on mostly crit and then heavy haste, with Versatility as the fallback if mana is a real problem, and adds that 12.1's Innervate is "probably better than it has ever been" for the spec. On hero talents he recommends Totemic: Farseer beat his expectations and can match or exceed its healing, but is far more punishing under movement and overlapping cooldown resets, where Totemic "practically plays itself". He makes no comparison against other healers.

takes.creator: Obli
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his Season 2 DPS Death Knight tier list, ranking the spec/hero-tree combinations against each other
takes.claim: He ranks Rider Frost the best Death Knight specialisation for Season 2 by a clear margin, putting it alone at the top of his list. His case is that it is doing very well on the PTR, carries good damage with significant burst roughly every 90 seconds, and — unlike Deathbringer — keeps more consistent damage outside its cooldown windows, while playing far more simply: the opener is straightforward, there is no Exterminate buff to track, and the rotation does not change whether or not the Riders are out. He rates Deathbringer Frost third and explicitly not bad, praising its 45-second burst window as handy for a lot of content but arguing it loses power on longer fights and is punishing if the second window does not arrive. The one hard condition he attaches: Rider Frost needs the new raid two-piece and one-handed weapons, so he tells viewers not to play Frost without it and to switch to it only once they have it. He rates only the DPS specs and states outright that he is not covering Blood.

takes.creator: Obli
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his Season 2 DPS Death Knight tier list, ranking the spec/hero-tree combinations against each other
takes.claim: He places Rider Unholy second, in A tier, and makes it his explicit patch-day recommendation: because Rider Frost depends on the new raid two-piece, he tells viewers to play Unholy at launch and switch once they have the set and one-handed weapons. On the spec itself he is positive — great damage, a simpler rotation than the Sandlane build because there is no Essence of the Blood Queen buff to maintain, more mobility, and damage he rates as equal to or better than Sandlane for an easier time. He is markedly negative on Sandlane Unholy specifically, not on the spec: it demands tank coordination to hold the Blood Queen buff, is hard to rebuild once dropped, and is not worth forcing yourself into a harder version of the spec for minimal or no gain when Rider Unholy does comparable damage in keys. He allows Sandlane could see raid play, where constant combat makes the buff easier to hold, and could do very well if there are execute damage amplifiers.

takes.creator: Bansherz
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 Marksmanship Hunter guide (rework, tier set and hero-tree read; complements, not replaces, his 08-07 M+ tier read)
takes.claim: He describes 12.1 as another soft rework for Marksmanship, centred on Explosive Shot: it now detonates every second it is on the target rather than once at the end, with two new talents beneath it — one allowing a second cast, which he calls really strong, and one adding a second of duration and therefore another explosion. Bullet Storm now buffs the next Aimed Shot after Rapid Fire instead of extending a duration, Wind's Quiver is redesigned around Rapid Fire, Aspect of the Hydra no longer affects Arcane Shot, and Double Tap is gone entirely, which he reads as too hard to balance. He rates the two-piece pretty good (a further second on Explosive Shot plus 5% more damage) and the four-piece nice, with flat Aimed and Rapid Fire damage and Explosive Shot reducing both cooldowns. Against that he calls the relocation of Tenacious and Cunning bad for the spec — previously taken automatically on the way to True Shot, it is now a real choice between losing damage and being too squishy, which he characterises as a loss either way. On hero trees he judges Dark Ranger too far behind numerically to touch: the talent and tier-set changes push you toward Sentinel, which is also tanky enough that Dark Ranger's defensives no longer justify it, though he notes the Black Arrow proc is now telegraphed by a buff rather than random, which he rates a nice quality-of-life gain.

takes.creator: VooDooSaurus
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his Season 2 Devourer guide as the Wowhead and Icy Veins Devourer guide writer (recorded 2026-08-09)
takes.claim: He calls Devourer pretty different in 12.1 and makes Void Scourge his recommended build for every situation — single target, party damage and overall damage profile all favour it, and he says it is significantly better than Annihilator in raid and in every situation once a live bug is fixed. That bug is the same haste/GCD double-apply he reported earlier, still present in game at recording: Cull, Reap, Devour and Consume take double the intended haste effect, which he says is pushing Annihilator higher than intended and is the only reason it is close in Mythic+. He tells viewers they can play Annihilator meanwhile, particularly on large pulls, and puts its crossover at roughly ten to twelve targets and above. He is clearly negative on Collapsing Star after its nerfs — very poorly tuned, poor synergy with the Void Scourge tree, no longer top damage, and a button he instructs Void Scourge players never to press. Against that he rates the tier set super powerful, saying it drives a lot of Reap damage and genuinely changes the rotation. He also flags that the optimal AoE pattern involves dropping Unrestrained Fury to cycle Void Metamorphosis windows faster and deliberately pressing nothing at the end of each window, and notes Blizzard has said they dislike this and intend to fix it in a future patch.

takes.creator: Jedith
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his Season 2 Annihilator Devourer guide, deliberately covering the caster build ahead of the Void Scourge guides
takes.claim: He argues the Annihilator caster build is more viable than the community initially concluded: after recent discoveries it is behind by only a couple of percent in AoE, which he calls not much in the grand scheme, and he tells viewers the playstyle is totally viable and still very competitive, especially in Mythic+, where he expects a lot of people to keep playing it. He reads the 12.1 changes as an improvement to the spec's feel: some damage has been moved out of the Void Metamorphosis windows into the out-of-meta windows for more even and reliable output, though he is careful to say a lot of damage still sits inside meta and centres on Collapsing Star. He rates the tier set very highly — the two-piece gives harvesting four or more fragments with Reap a 20% chance to make the next Consume instant and explode, and the four-piece grants eight fragments plus 20% increased Reap damage — and says the practical effect is pressing Reap almost as often as Consume, so that Consume spam is a thing of the past. He confirms Collapsing Star was nerfed but, unlike the Void Scourge build, still calls it the main bread and butter at high target counts. This is a different lens from VooDooSaurus's same-week read, which puts Annihilator behind Void Scourge in all situations.

takes.creator: LBNinja7
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his Season 2 Mythic+ Mistweaver guide, tracing the full PTR tuning arc (complements his 08-02 M+ healer tier-list placement)
takes.claim: Walking through the whole PTR tuning arc for keys he describes a spec pulled in two directions. On the gain side, mastery — the spot heals that proc from applying a mist or kicking up an ally — was buffed twice, the second time by a further 50%, which he calls much more healing than Season 1 and later a gigabuff; Jadefire Teachings was buffed, deliberately incentivising the single-target rotation over Spinning Crane Kick spam. On the loss side he lists a 3% cut followed by a further 8% nerf to everything outside damage-conversion healing, a Spinning Crane Kick nerf to both its damage and its healing component, and a 60% cut to Morning Breeze, which took Rising Sun Kick's mastery scaling from 20% to 8% and pulled the spec back off the mastery path it had been driven down for most of the PTR. He says those active-healing nerfs hit Shaolin's Gift hard enough that the third point is no longer affordable, with Spirit Font stepping in for spot healing. The tier set pivots from Renewing Mist to Rising Sun Kick — 30% more damage plus a chance to reset its own cooldown — and he says the practical consequence is that the rotation is genuinely target-count dependent again rather than Spinning Crane Kick dominating. Stats are haste, then crit, then mastery, then versatility. He ends positive on how it plays, saying he is excited for the single-target rotation and more healing on boss fights, and keeps a high-mastery build on the fringe as viable if gear supplies the stat.

takes.creator: Tactyks
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his Season 2 Protection Paladin guide, raid build and tier-set section (complements, not replaces, his 08-09 raid tank tier-list placement)
takes.claim: He reads the Season 2 spec-tree rework as a deliberate move of power out of the Avenging Wrath window and into the baseline spec, and is explicit that it cuts both ways for raid. The cost: Avenging Wrath's damage, healing and crit bonus are halved from 20% to 10%, and Sanctified Wrath is removed entirely, so wings run shorter and Judgment gives one Holy Power instead of two inside them — a hit he calls fairly significant and says will be felt hardest at launch before item level partly compensates. He also flags a more than 50% cut to Reflection of Radiance's proc rate as a very large nerf that brings Lightsmith's wings uptime down toward Templar's, and notes Word of Glory did not receive the compensation healing other abilities got for the patch-wide 25% health increase, leaving it relatively weaker than in Season 1. Against that he rates the baseline spec stronger defensively: the new Seal of Reprisal gives a 10% damage reduction on anything hit by Blessed Hammer, the reworked Word of Glory no longer crits but scales with crit chance and converts 80% of overhealing into an absorb, Bulwark and Undying Embers are buffed, and Paladin double-dips the compensation healing because those heals scale off the buffed Avenger's Shield and Consecration damage. On the tier set he is positive but measured — a 30% larger Consecration granting 5% increased crit chance against enemies standing in it, and 20% additional Holy damage from Judgment and Blessed Hammer that doubles on a critical strike — calling it a pretty substantial throughput boost and a solid set, though not the best, and purely offensive. He rates stats haste first, then crit, then versatility, with mastery last and still unreliable after no rework.

takes.creator: Tactyks
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his Season 2 Protection Paladin guide, Mythic+ build section (complements, not replaces, his 08-09 M+ tank tier-list placement)
takes.claim: For keys he generally recommends Lightsmith but is emphatic that Templar is equally viable — he says there is no problem playing it and that you can have just as much success, partly because there is a lot of empty space in this season's dungeons, which hurts Shake the Heavens uptime. He stresses the left side of the tree is unchanged from Season 1, so the familiar flex points remain, and singles out Righteous Protection as a niche pick this season because of the number of poison dispels in the dungeon pool. The rework's practical effect on keys is that Instrument of the Divine moves out of the capstone into the middle of the tree, which he says makes it a mainstay of essentially every build since the capstone was always too tight to afford it in Mythic+; it lets Shield of the Righteous consume five Holy Power for extra damage, with the caveat that fishing for five risks losing the defensive uptime. He gives two specific new-tool instructions for pulls: use Blessed Hammer early to get the 10% Seal of Reprisal damage reduction rolling before grouping, and spend spare Word of Glory procs on yourself for the overheal absorb to smooth the initial grouping. He expects key-pushing Protection Paladins to favour the haste-proc sword from the final boss over the higher-damage axe and trinket set combo, because the single-target damage procs matter far less in keys and the set eats a trinket slot for no defensive value. He notes the rotation itself is essentially unchanged from Season 1.

takes.creator: Publik
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his Season 2 Shadow Priest guide (supersedes his 06-21 initial-build reads, several of whose numbers he revises here)
takes.claim: He is strongly positive on Shadow's Season 2 direction, saying the changes are focused and targeted and cover a lot of what the community has asked for, and calling it possibly the most fun Shadow playstyle in a while. He revises his own June figure for the new Shade Burst talent upward: rather than the 2-3% he measured on the initial build, it is now doing roughly 5-6% of damage in single target and more in AoE, giving the spec a stable AoE anchor so Psychic Link no longer has to absorb constant tuning, and letting Shadow damage small adds without dotting them. Void Form is reworked so Void Volley has three uses per window instead of a cooldown, which he says removes the rigid pressure to fire the first one immediately and makes the playstyle much more forgiving. Ancient Madness is redesigned to stack 2% haste and 1.5 seconds of Void Form duration per Shadow Word: Madness up to five times, with the haste lingering and decaying over ten seconds afterwards, giving back a ramping feel — and he notes the consequence that pure single-target haste value falls slightly while crit rises.
