He also revises his June read of the tier set from lukewarm to excited: the two-piece takes three seconds off Tentacle Slam and doubles its damage, and the four-piece grants a free full-effectiveness Void Volley from every Tentacle Slam, which changes the opener (open Mind Blast rather than Tentacle Slam) and makes Tentacle Slam a genuine damage button rather than an afterthought. He cautions that trinkets are undertuned and expects further tuning after release.

takes.creator: Publik
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his Season 2 Shadow Priest guide, hero-tree comparison (supersedes his 06-21 read that Archon was 15%+ ahead)
takes.claim: On hero trees he keeps Archon ahead of Voidweaver but in far more measured terms than his June read, which had put Archon roughly 15% or more ahead in all content on the back of Focused Outburst. Here he says Voidweaver is still looking a little under Archon in single target and that he does not expect it to see a lot of raid play, while providing a Voidweaver build for anyone who wants it and noting the Mythic+ gap is small enough that the build differs from Archon's by essentially one talent. He describes the Archon changes as consolidating rather than inflating: Focused Outburst is redesigned so Void Volley deals a flat 15% more damage and Shadow Word: Madness during Void Form unleashes a reduced-effectiveness Void Volley, which he explicitly identifies as a tuning knob; and Resonant Energy is reworked from a Halo-applied debuff into a stacking self-buff, which he welcomes mainly as a consistency fix because Halo sometimes missed targets. He is candid that he expects post-release tuning to move these rankings.

takes.creator: Harrek
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — live read-through of the Restoration Shaman rework patch notes (superseded by his 08-08 Dummy Dome read)
takes.claim: Reading the Restoration Shaman rework notes unrehearsed, he is emphatically positive, saying he has no idea where the spec lands on balance but thinks it is absurdly strong, expects incredible buffs to show on the following PTR builds, and closes with zero complaints, zero notes. The specifics he singles out: Riptide's direct healing up 25% and its periodic healing doubled, fixing what he calls a centrepiece talent that was weak at actually healing and only existed to proc other effects; a new Swirling Tides talent letting Healing Stream and Storm Stream Totem extend active Riptides by three seconds, which he rates highly because more Riptide uptime compounds into Tidal Waters and Undercurrent; Healing Rain now hitting six targets, which he reads as a deliberately raid-targeted change because Shaman was struggling in raid but not in Mythic+; Earthen Accord becoming an additive 20% so Unleash Life's bonus goes from 25% to 45% rather than 30%; and Unleash Life's baseline healing doubled to cover the loss of the Season 1 tier set. On Farseer he says the ancestors' Chain Heal now bouncing to five targets instead of three and losing 10% per jump instead of 30%, on top of a 50% baseline Chain Heal increase, roughly triples ancestor Chain Heal output and is exactly what the tree needed. He is content with the tier set being nerfed, on the grounds that power moving from random procs to spells the player chooses to press is where he wants it.

takes.creator: Harrek
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his read of the first 12.1 PTR patch notes, before the July rework (superseded by his 07-22 and 08-08 reads, which reverse this verdict)
takes.claim: On the first 12.1 PTR notes he is downbeat about Restoration Shaman in raid, expecting it to be just okay: not a troll pick, since it brings the Shaman buff, Spirit Link and an appropriate amount of healing, but with no real reason to bring one over another healer unless the buff is needed. He says he expects the spec to remain roughly bottom of the barrel in pure healing throughput and that the new tier set does not fix that. He is disappointed that the only class-specific line in the notes is Healing Rain gaining a 12-second cooldown and 18-second duration — a change he had specifically asked for and likes for Farseer flexibility, but which he says should have arrived mid-Season 1 rather than as the sole change going into a new season. On the tier set he measures the two-piece proc rate as very low in early testing, roughly one extra Healing Rain a minute, and calls the four-piece shield very weak at around 2,000 HPS against 800,000 player health. His one positive note is that the extra Healing Rain can be abused for double Downpour and extra Tidal Waters procs, which he rates as strong in raid but niche and RNG-dependent, and he says making the set work properly would be a large boon to Shaman in raid without affecting Mythic+ much. This read is entirely reversed by his 07-22 reaction to the July rework.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his Season 2 Holy Priest guide, raid section (complements, not replaces, his 08-08 raid spec-choice read)
takes.claim: For raid he recommends Archon over Oracle without qualification, saying that across all their raid testing, Dummy Dome testing and other testing Archon was still pulling ahead by a sizable margin even though Oracle's passive healing is quite strong, and he rates the burst potential extremely valuable. The 12.1 changes he identifies are gains: Apotheosis now cuts Holy Word mana cost by 70% rather than 50%, Divine Hymn has been upgraded to grant Guardian Spirit for its channel — a cheat death he rates as a way to immune mechanics outright — and the rank-three Apex talent is made reliable, with Serenity now giving a guaranteed Benediction upgrade on the next Flash Heal rather than a chance. The two-piece grants up to 6% crit from targets carrying your Renew and the four-piece adds 10% Renew healing plus a guaranteed Renew from Light's Resurgence, which he characterises as more passive output. His stated constraint throughout is mana: Prayer of Healing is expensive enough that Archon's whole game is weaving Smites to fish Surge of Light procs, helped by Everlasting Light raising that chance as mana drops, and he warns that overcapping Benediction stacks inside an Apotheosis window is an easy way to drain mana. Raid stats are crit first, then versatility and mastery equally, then haste.

takes.creator: AutomaticJak
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his Season 2 Holy Priest guide, Mythic+ section (complements, not replaces, his 08-08 M+ healer testing read)
takes.claim: For keys he recommends Oracle at time of recording, saying PTR testing showed it much more mana efficient and consistent across the heal checks they met, and that Oracle specifically can exceed expectations in heavy rot damage because its passive healing and constant output are very strong. The build is a Renew engine: Ultimate Serenity drops Sanctify to make Serenity cleave, Lasting Words then applies six seconds of Renew to every ally it heals, Light's Resurgence plus the four-piece keeps Renew rolling from Prayer of Mending, and Renewed Faith adds 10% healing to anyone carrying it — so the two-piece crit bonus is close to permanently active. He also credits Oracle-specific buffs to Prompt Prognosis and to Prayer of Mending's efficiency in five-player content. Against that he is direct about the spec's standing weaknesses in dungeons rather than any 12.1 change: he calls lack of survivability one of Holy Priest's biggest downsides, says its utility is usually not as strong in a dungeon environment as many other specs, and names two-to-three target cleave as one of the toughest areas for the spec to succeed in — advising Guardian Spirit be used to deprioritise one target when cleave healing outstrips throughput. Key stats are crit, then versatility and haste, then mastery, with versatility gaining value at high keys for the survivability.

takes.creator: Critcake
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — launch-eve stream, reading the completed Season 2 Arms tuning arc (Slayer build; supersedes his 07-09 broader Arms read)
takes.claim: Walking through the finished tuning arc he concludes Arms is actually really strong now and that it is a good time to play Slayer Arms, saying it feels amazing on the PTR. He traces how it got there: large buffs first — auto attack damage increased by 100%, a much higher Slayer Strike proc chance, a buffed two-piece, a stronger Opportunist and a substantially stronger Dreadnought on multi-target though not single target — after which the sims came back showing execute damage and overall damage both very high, so Blizzard trimmed execute and Powerful Momentum and buffed Forethought partly to offset the execute cut. The gameplay consequence he emphasises is proc density: the higher Slayer Strike rate feeds many more Sudden Death procs, and Tactical Edge was reworked to guarantee a Sudden Death proc on every Colossal Smash. This is a launch-eve stream rather than a guide, and he says plainly that he has deliberately not studied the season in depth yet and is only now reading through a written guide on stream.

takes.creator: Critcake
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — launch-eve stream, answering a viewer directly on whether Fury is bad in Season 2
takes.claim: Asked directly by a viewer whether Fury is bad next season, he says he does not think it is bad and that people are underestimating it precisely because Arms is totally in the spotlight. He treats the perception gap as the story rather than the numbers, joking that it is better not to talk Fury up — if the community keeps believing it is weak, it is more likely to be buffed, and he says he would not mind ending up in a Fury season either. He offers no throughput figures or testing to support the read, so this is a contrarian perception call from a Warrior main rather than a measured comparison, recorded as neutral for that reason.

takes.creator: Dalaran Gaming
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — patch-day release stream, playing the Season 2 rebuild of the spec
takes.claim: He is unreservedly positive on the Season 2 rebuild: Killing Spree was buffed heavily and, combined with routing it through the drone-rush supercharger, Outlaw finally has a real burst window instead of purely sustained damage. He also notes the talent tree gained connectors that make builds easier to path. Levelling a rogue on the spec, he repeatedly calls the new flow the most fun part of the patch for him and expects viewers to enjoy it, though he ties none of this to throughput numbers.

takes.creator: Dalaran Gaming
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — patch-day release stream, answering viewers on Subtlety's Season 2 standing
takes.claim: A two-sided read. He says long-standing Subtlety bugs went unfixed in Season 1 and were compensated with buffs, whereas this time the spec was nerfed instead — and that it is now locked into the Deathstalker hero tree, which he thinks plays poorly in M+ and leaves the rotation unchanged and boring. Against that he still expects it to be good on paper and notes rogues carried few structural changes from Season 1, so he does not call it weak, only unappealing and worse-treated than before.

takes.creator: Dalaran Gaming
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — patch-day release stream, advising viewers picking one rogue spec for the season
takes.claim: Asked what to pick, he offers Assassination as the safe default rather than the strongest choice, reasoning that a spec built around cooldowns tends to survive tuning better. He is explicit that tuning is not final and that nobody knows the meta pick yet, and he hedges his own PTR/raid-testing read with 'should not be terrible, if it is not bugged'. He also says Deathstalker is significantly ahead of Fadebound for the spec. Recorded neutral because he declines to make a strength claim.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 healer prep stream, revisiting his own healer tier list
takes.claim: He walks back his own placement from roughly eleven days earlier, saying he put too much emphasis on Mistweaver and would now put it around B tier. Pressed on whether it is genuinely bad, he separates the brackets: not that bad in M+, where he argues a lot of healers sit at similar power, but possibly weak in raid. He had expected buffs to the spec's Sheilun's/Vivify line before launch, says they have not arrived, and still expects them before the raid opens — so the read is a downgrade held open pending tuning rather than a settled negative.

takes.creator: Shadarek
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — pre-season video on what he is playing, with an explicit refusal to forecast the meta
takes.claim: Under current tuning he says Devourer is ahead of Havoc, while stressing he cannot say what will be meta and that weekly tuning is expected for three or four more weeks — he explicitly declines to guess. On hero trees, Void's Guard is significantly ahead in pure single target and roughly level with Annihilator once cleave is involved, so near-identical for M+; he is nonetheless playing Annihilator because Void's Guard forces a ranged spec into melee and he finds it uncomfortable and exposed to range mechanics. He also notes the carried-over tier set keys off Collapsing Star and so does nothing for Void's Guard.

takes.creator: Shadarek
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — pre-season video on what he is playing, with an explicit refusal to forecast the meta
takes.claim: He places Havoc behind Devourer under current tuning but is careful to say it is not unviable and remains good, with Season 1 builds still fine to carry into pre-season. He sees no reason to chase Essence Break until the tier set lands. His broader advice for the week is to play what you enjoy rather than the optimal pick, since M0 is trivial content and tuning will move repeatedly before it matters.

takes.creator: Tactyks
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his Season 2 Guardian Druid guide: patch changes, tier set and raid build (M+ section firewalled out — he authors the Method M+ tier list already in the consensus)
takes.claim: His first Guardian read under the widened scope, from a guide rather than a tier list — a changes assessment, not a placement. He reads the patch's blanket percentage tuning as net neutral (compensation for the global 25% health increase) and locates the real movement in three places. The apex talent's full rework from burst toward sustain is a redesign he says he is a fan of: its passives add 6% mastery and Mangle damage, and its final rank resets Thrash and Mangle, amps both by 30% while a spirit is active, and refunds rage — so Mangle is, in his words, definitely back in the conversation after the never-hitting-Mangle end of Season 1. Against that sits the one significant nerf he flags: Lunation becomes a flat 20-second cooldown reduction on Lunar Beam (40 seconds flat, versus sub-30 before), a meaningful uptime loss he calls a pain point but not the end of the world, partly shored up by the tier set's four-piece extending Incarnation toward 35 seconds. For raid specifically he still runs Alune's Chosen — with an explicit on-camera plea for Blizzard to buff Druid of the Claw's damage, which he says otherwise feels bad to play — describes the raid build as a damage/defense hybrid little changed from Season 1, keeps Maul in the raid rotation (unlike keys), and calls out the Ula'tek weapon, a two-socket crit neck and, oddly, the Feral set-bonus trinket off the guillotine boss as standout raid loot, the last being Guardian's best-in-slot damage trinket even though Guardian cannot complete its set. He also notes Maul, Raze and Ravage remain undertuned after the old apex's compensation nerfs and hopes that gets addressed.

takes.creator: NeekapHere
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his full Season 2 Retribution Paladin PvE guide (stats, both hero-talent builds, ability priority, tier set and best-in-slot)
takes.claim: He ends the guide with an explicit verdict — Retribution is fun to play but 'a little bit weak right now', hoping tuning fixes it — and the reason he gives is the Season 2 tier set. The four-piece grants Divine Arbiter when you spend a different spender than the one Divine Purpose procced on, but he says simulations are now in and the arbiter's damage is not high enough to justify the swap: on Templar single target the arbiter never beats Final Verdict, so you simply never press Divine Storm and never use the set at all, which he calls a huge issue. He reports the same problem on Templar AoE and Herald AoE, leaving Herald single target as the only case where the set works the way it is meant to. He had raised this on the PTR and says the fix that shipped — Divine Arbiter benefiting from Divine Purpose and Greater Judgment — was not close to his proposed solution and is not good enough. In Mythic+ the set is partially usable: on two to four targets spending Final Verdict off the proc is a real damage gain, and on larger packs you can still route it into a priority target, but on true mass AoE you go back to spamming Divine Storm and drop the set again. On builds he rates Templar slightly ahead of Herald in both single target and keys, but inside margin of error and close enough to play either. Stats are strength, then mastery, with crit and haste roughly equal (crit favoured in keys and on Templar, haste on single-target Herald) and versatility last. He says he expects to publish an update video if the tier set is retuned.

takes.creator: Shadarek
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — his Season 2 Havoc Demon Hunter raiding and Mythic+ guide (changes, hero-talent builds, tier set, gearing and rotation)
takes.claim: He opens by saying Havoc is looking to be pretty good for raid coming into 12.1, and good for Mythic+ too with the caveat that Devourer may simply overshadow it there. The centrepiece is Essence Break: its initial hit was buffed by almost 50%, the tier set adds 12% from the two-piece and another 35% to the initial hit on the four-piece, extends its duration from four to six seconds and cuts the cooldown from 40 to 30 seconds — over double the old initial damage — which is why he now presses it on cooldown and why the whole season's build is arranged around it. Other gains: the dead Dash of Chaos talent was replaced with Never Say Die (3% damage above 50% health, leech below it, in practice a damage increase), Trail of Ruin became flat damage rather than a dot, Serrated Glaive moved from an enemy debuff to a self-buff that is permanently up, and Blade Dance, Death Sweep, Chaos Strike and Annihilation all took small buffs. Against that he flags real losses: Immolation Aura's fury generation dropped from 40 to 30 and Blind Fury was nerfed again, so Havoc is now noticeably more reliant on a shaman's fury economy; Inertia was cut to 12% for five seconds because the compensating duration increase was never applied, which he calls a massive nerf that makes it unplayable; and the global 25% player health increase indirectly devalues leech to roughly 80% of its old power, so the spec feels less tanky even though he still rates it incredibly tanky overall. On builds he says the pure single-target Fel-Scarred build sims best for that hero tree but still sims slightly below Aldrachi Reaver and is only worth considering on the raid's one true single-target fight, so he expects cleave-oriented builds in practice; Aldrachi Reaver's Mythic+ build is identical to its raid build bar one talent swap, and Trail of Ruin is dropped in both.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 launch-day healer stream, answering a viewer comparing Discipline and Holy Priest (raid half of the read)
takes.claim: Asked to compare the two Priest healers, he reads Discipline as very strong in raid — his words are that Disc is 'insane in raid' — and draws the forward-looking conclusion that it is more likely to be nerfed than buffed. He frames this as a standing design problem rather than a passing tuning state: Blizzard has struggled to buff Discipline for Mythic+ without also buffing it in raid, so the raid strength is what blocks help arriving for keys. Recorded as a strength read on the raid bracket, with the nerf expectation as his own hedge rather than an observed change.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 launch-day healer stream, answering a viewer comparing Discipline and Holy Priest (Mythic+ half of the read)
takes.claim: For keys specifically he says he does not think Discipline is in a good state, and advises a viewer who plays only Mythic+ not to put their eggs in the Disc basket. His reasoning is that the spec's raid strength makes a Mythic+ buff unlikely — Blizzard cannot lift it for keys without lifting it in raid, where he thinks it could use a nerf — so he expects the key-facing weakness to persist rather than be tuned away. He explicitly contrasts it with Holy Priest, which he says he would pick over Disc for keys in the specs' current state.

takes.creator: MadSkillzzTV
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 launch-day healer stream, on Holy Paladin's Mythic+ standing at patch launch
takes.claim: His first read from live 12.1 rather than the PTR, and it is strongly positive: he calls Holy Paladin very strong in Mythic+, saying it moves health bars like no other healer. He also describes the wider reaction — that the spec is 'the latest hotness' and the subject of an enormous volume of meta coverage, that people are already afraid it will be nerfed, and that he expects everyone to level one. His own position is that he hopes the nerf does not come and that Holy Paladin deserves its time in the sun after a long stretch out of favour; later in the stream he reacts to the possibility of a 10% healing nerf with dismay. Recorded as a strength read; the nerf talk is anticipation of tuning, not an observed change.

takes.creator: Bansherz
takes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 day-two stream, a boss-by-boss raid read on the three Hunter specs (complements, not replaces, his 08-11 Marksmanship guide)
takes.claim: Going through the new raid boss by boss he concludes that Marksmanship is, in his words, king in the raid — 'pretty insane on all the fights' so far — with the two-target cleave profile of several encounters suiting it particularly well. He is careful about the fights he has not tested: on the last boss he could see any of the three Hunter specs being the pick, guessing Beast Mastery may be poor there because platform movement will hurt pet AI, that Survival may fit because the fight rewards priority damage and add killing, and that Marksmanship may benefit for the same pet-AI reason. He separates this from keys explicitly, where he ranks the three the other way and very close together: Survival slightly best by fractions of a percent, Beast Mastery a couple of percent ahead of Marksmanship, and Survival becoming really strong in keys once the tier set is online. Recorded on the raid bracket only, since his Mythic+ ordering puts Marksmanship last of the three.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Frost DK as the clear standout of the raid testing — the one outlier that sits at or near the top of essentially every boss regardless of whether the fight wants single target, cleave or AoE. He credits its free passive AoE (Icy Death Torrent auto-attack cleave) for letting it excel on single-target fights without giving anything up, and names it the overall best DPS so far.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen puts Frost Mage among the top three overall DPS in the testing, driven mainly by its strong two-target cleave, which shone on the cleave-heavy fights like Twin Fangs and the Lost Explorers council.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen rates Shadow Priest as one of the best overall performers, valued for its multi-target/multi-dot flexibility — it held up on the caster AoE opener, was the biggest non-Frost-DK outlier on the two-target Tomb Sentinels, and reached five-target spread cleave on Twin Fangs.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen highlights Arms Warrior as a strong overall performer thanks to its very good two-target cleave from Sweeping Strikes, which gave it value on the council and Twin Fangs fights, and it also placed among the top melee on the movement-heavy single-target boss.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen sees Affliction as a strong AoE/multi-dot pick that performed well on caster-and-spread fights — the add-heavy opener, the council (agony/corruption across three targets), and Twin Fangs' five-target spread. He notes it's less ideal on pure single target, since it has to actively cast for its AoE rather than getting it for free, but overall counts it among the better specs.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen counts BM Hunter among the strong overall performers and calls it the 'melee-adopted' ranged spec — fully mobile with instant abilities, so it topped the movement-heavy pure-single-target fight (Zoroak) alongside the melee where static casters struggled.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen lists Havoc among the better overall DPS of the testing, and it appeared near the top of the movement-heavy single-target fight where mobile melee were favored.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen says Arcane Mage was doing very well on the caster-friendly fights — the sustained-AoE opener and the stationary single-target boss (Bashnik) — because it picks up free AoE through Arcane Missiles/Barrage and the prismatic-bolt splash while doing its single-target rotation.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen names Balance among the casters favored on the sustained-AoE opener (Nexali) and includes it in the five-target spread-cleave group that thrives on Twin Fangs, so he reads it as well-positioned on the multi-target fights.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen lists Elemental among the casters doing well on the large sustained-AoE opener (Nexali), where slow ramping multi-target damage is rewarded.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen calls Preservation Evoker the clear best healer in the testing — practically the only spec pushing toward ~300k HPS. He credits the big Dream Breath heal-over-time buff (average ~1.2M per HoT cast) plus the new tier set's Sea of Essence bursts, which have pushed it into a Flame Shaper build.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Discipline as essentially unchanged — still an atonement spec, with Blizzard continuing to shift power toward Void Shield and away from atonement, a trend that isn't reversing in the patch. He frames it as static rather than improving.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen sees Mistweaver as unchanged — same very high APM, same three-ability rotation cadence, and the same hero-talent/talent setup, with no meaningful shift in how it plays or performs.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen groups Holy Priest with the healers that were performing horribly in the testing; it has only been buffed 'a bit,' leaving it well behind the standout Preservation.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen counts Holy Paladin among the healers that were doing badly in the raid testing, receiving only a small buff so far and still lagging the top healers.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Frost DK as looking strong for S2 M+ — it is far and away the most-played DPS in the PTR. He credits the rework: the burst window (Pillar of Frost, Breath, Obliterate) was nerfed while passive damage like Howling Blast, Icy Death Torrent and Remorseless Winter was roughly doubled, and it is putting up top results. He cautions the heavy play partly reflects excitement over big changes, but the parses back it up.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Unholy as staying meta and strong into S2, but sees it as the less exciting DK — its PTR changes look long on paper yet barely alter the playstyle, so fewer players are testing it versus the more heavily reworked Frost.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Arcane as looking strong and among the most-played DPS in PTR M+. He points to an Apex rework adding Prismatic Bolt (now the hardest-hitting ability) and a new tier set that pulls Arcane Missiles back into the core AoE rotation, driving both strong results and player hype.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Fire Mage as weak — he flatly says Fire and Frost are 'down there because they're bad, especially Fire Mage,' which is why Mage interest has shifted entirely to Arcane.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Frost Mage as bad/weak for S2, lumping it with Fire as the underperforming Mage specs players are abandoning in favor of the reworked Arcane.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen notes Guardian is the reigning meta tank yet the least-played tank in the PTR — not from any tuning knock, but because it is overshadowed by the newly buffed Prot Paladin soaking up all the interest.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Prot Paladin as the standout tank for S2, by far the most-played, thanks to a large pile of defensive buffs: Ardent Defender granting +20% max HP and now keeping its buffs through the cheat-death proc, the now-fixed Silver Reprisal, plus more self-healing from Avenger's Shield, Consecration and a much-improved Word of Glory.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Aug as still strong (hence still popular) but not improved — it gets almost no tuning, loses a powerful S1 tier set for roughly a wash, and takes an M+ nerf now that its Apex no longer grants free knock-up crowd control. Nothing to be excited about.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Marksmanship as trending up — after its latest changes (including repeated Explosive Shot buffs) it has climbed in both play rate and results, doing very well especially in AoE, and is now a genuine alternative to BM.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads BM as looking good — it was already the stronger Hunter spec by default, and its tier set makes Cobra Shot (an already-frequent filler) its strongest button, without changing the rotation.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Affliction as the dominant, most-played Warlock in PTR M+ results and top damage — but he is puzzled, because it is one of the least-changed specs (only minor tier-set buffs to Agony/Corruption), so its strength is not really coming from S2 tuning.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Havoc as looking good, holding near-equal damage and popularity with Devourer despite receiving little tuning focus — its 4-piece tier set brings back Essence Break, a ~40s burst window that lines up perfectly with M+ pulls.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Devourer as looking good for S2, sitting near-equal to Havoc in both damage and popularity — it got the biggest rework, with a large mastery/in-meta damage nerf offset by a flat 20% buff to everything else plus a 'very cool' new tier set.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Mistweaver as remaining one of the two most-popular healers, carrying over its established S1 strength with nothing notable changed.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Disc as a top-popularity healer for S2, played into far more and much higher keys than a struggling spec like Preservation.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen lists Resto Shaman among the still-popular, 'still here' healers alongside Mistweaver and Disc, but gives it no individual read — essentially unchanged from S1.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Preservation as improving but still weak in M+ — historically poor and still stuck in few, low keys far behind other healers, though it gets another round of helpful changes (low-target healing QOL, plus a tier set granting extra Essence Bursts and a 150% Chrono Flame). Nowhere near the hype of Prot Pal, Frost DK or Arcane.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Reads Frost DK as the dominant PTR performer — showing up constantly in top M+ keys and strong in raid, the best of all melee alongside Unholy — and calls its huge nerf (he estimates roughly 20% single-target, ~17% AoE effective) the most deserved of the round.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Warns not to assume Unholy was weak just because Frost stood out: in raid testing Unholy was the spec appearing most in single-target and 2-3 target results (especially the season's pure single-target boss), among the best melee — hence a roughly 15% nerf hitting its core pet damage.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Sees Havoc as having been doing okay on the PTR — clearly better than Devourer but not at the nerfed DKs' level — and finds its 5% nerf a bit surprising.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Says Devourer's rework direction was praised but its actual damage was low — effectively nerfed compared to live — so the 10% buff is Blizzard trying to bump an underperformer up.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Reads Balance as well positioned for this raid: it wasn't awful in single target, the tested raid has few pure single-target fights, and Balance benefits from multi-target on many encounters — with the new buffs skewing AoE, he calls it a good change even if parts net out flat.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Judges the Scalecommander package to be in a pretty tough spot for Devastation after the Wingleader rework — decoupling the cooldown reduction from Bombardments is both a playstyle change and a significant net nerf in his view.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Extends the same read to Augmentation: the Wingleader rework leaves Scalecommander in a tough situation for both Evoker DPS specs, since the cooldown reduction is far less frequent than before.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Calls Preservation the best-performing healer in PTR raid testing by a reasonable margin — essentially the only healer clearing the top HPS benchmarks — driven by the Dream Breath HoT rebalance, so the broad nerf to that package was expected.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Reads BM's changes as roughly a 10%+ net nerf that lands badly: BM was doing decently in single target but quite poorly in AoE, and the round guts its single-target strengths (Cobra Shot package, tier set halved) while giving nothing for the weak AoE.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Says Marksmanship wasn't performing nearly as well as BM, particularly in single target, and calls its broad ~8-10% buff (everything except Aimed/Explosive Shot) quite good for the spec.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Reads Fire as doing extremely low damage across the board on the PTR and being barely played in testing — the ~12% buff is Blizzard trying to revive a spec players weren't even bothering to try.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Considers Windwalker to be doing okay damage-wise — not in a poor spot — but as traditionally one of the squishiest specs, he sees the stamina and damage-reduction buffs as a needed defensive fix rather than a throughput change.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Calls Holy Paladin one of the biggest winners — a second consecutive round of large buffs to spenders, all healing, and the tier set — though he flags a design worry that the buffed, infusion-empowered single-target spender is now so strong it threatens to make Holy Shock obsolete until a follow-up rebalance.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Flags Protection Paladin as a potential meta pick: it kept its double round of buffs without a nerf, and PTR M+ tanks already pushing 18-20 keys are doing it on Prot Paladin — a strong hint about its power level.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Reads Holy Priest as one of the few healers failing the raid HPS benchmarks, with severe mana problems; the mana discounts and 10% healing buff help but skip its biggest mana drain, moving it from terrible to only slightly below average in his estimation.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Sees Shadow as already doing well — a major beneficiary of the many multi-target fights in this raid — and finds it curious that it's getting a further flat 8% buff anyway, though he notes it wasn't especially popular as a DPS pick.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Says the 8% Subtlety nerf makes no sense to him: Sub was not doing great in raid testing and was unpopular in M+, so unless Blizzard has a bigger rework planned, the spec is just left worse off.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Reads Affliction as having been around top-5 M+ damage, but largely via a degenerate tier-set interaction that let players skip casting Unstable Affliction entirely; the effectiveness cut from 50% to 20% closes that loophole and forces the real rotation back.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Calls Destruction the worst-performing spec alongside Fire Mage — very poor damage and very little play in testing — with the flat 10% buff as its only lifeline.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Reads Arms as notably weak in pure single-target raid fights while doing quite a bit better with cleave and in M+ AoE; the new buffs (execute, melee damage) deliberately target that single-target hole, worth roughly 5% ST and almost nothing in AoE.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen names Arcane Mage the clear standout of the PTR M+ so far — by far the most popular DPS (roughly doubling to tripling other specs in representation) and a very strong performer. The Prismatic Bolt Apex upgrade adds a huge chunk of damage, orb-mastery lets Arcane Orb consume Clearcasting, and the spec also gained strong defensive layers (extra barrier charge, flat AoE reduction), making it a prime meta candidate.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Frost DK as still one of the strongest M+ specs even after a 20%+ nerf five days ago — the nerf only brought it from far-and-away best to merely one of the best. Its rebuilt profile leans on passive AoE (Remorseless Winter / Icy Death Torrent, further reinforced by the tier set) while Obliterate and Glacial Advance drop in priority; a big change from Season 1 and a top PTR performer.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen highlights Elemental Shaman as drastically buffed and reworked for M+: the spec swings from its Stormbringer lightning build to a Farseer fire build (big base-spell buffs offsetting Ascendance nerfs, Voltaic Blaze enabling AoE Lava Bursts). It's doing very well in the PTR with strong AoE and strong priority/funnel damage.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen notes Balance Druid is doing quite well and is popular in higher M+ keys, and has been buffed to be numerically stronger — but stresses it plays essentially the same as it does on live (mostly flat damage-number changes), so he doesn't weight it as a major mover in the PTR M+ picture.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen has Devourer DH among the most popular M+ specs after its recent +10% buff, edging out Havoc. But its huge burst-window identity is much diminished from live — heavy mastery and Collapsing Star nerfs pushed many players off the Annihilator/collapsing-star build (especially in raid); it stays competitive in M+ where burst windows still pay off, just far less dominant than on live.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen notes Abundance was buffed (Regrowth crit chance and mana discount to 60% from 50%, plus +25% base Regrowth) to coax Resto Druid back onto Regrowth after Season 2 caps Abundance at 50% (down from 96%). Even post-buff it returns to roughly its current healing profile and remained one of the weaker — and less-popular — healers in the PTR raid testing.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen says Preservation was the most-popular and generally best-performing healer in the raid testing (top results, even on the actual kills), but took hefty nerfs — Dream Breath nerfed again plus its blessing (Nourish's/Ritual's) healing down — bringing it closer to the pack. It stays manageable because Echo/Temporal Anomaly let it pivot heal-duplication from Dream Breath onto Reversion.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen: Mistweaver, which was performing okay in testing (rarely top, rarely bottom), got an 8% across-the-board healing nerf paired with an odd +50% mastery buff — a stat Mistweaver has long disliked. The now effectively-doubled mastery softens the hit and adds future value, but it still nets to a nerf for the spec.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen calls Holy Paladin the most-buffed healer of the PTR cycle — successive rounds buffing healing, spenders, damage, Pillar of Light/Beacon passives, and now a +50% Holy Shock buff plus mana discount. The pile of buffs is strong enough that the no-Holy-Shock build (Holy Light → guaranteed Infusion → instant Flash of Light) still wins, so even the buffed Holy Shock isn't worth pressing.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen: Disc's Season 2 tuning pushes power from Void Shield back into Penance (Penance up, Shadow Mend spot healing up) while nerfing Atonement in raid (~7% less at 20 targets) and Void Shield — a net nerf in raid, roughly neutral in M+ where you actually use these. He likes the direction (curbing the Void-Shield value creep), though the tier set's guaranteed Void Shield on Mind Blast reset means you'll still cast more of them in Season 2.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen: Holy Priest is one of the more-buffed healers after Holy Paladin — +10% healing, mana discounts, and Benediction now cast about twice as often (tied to Holy Word/Serenity rather than Apotheosis), plus a smaller latest round buffing Prayer of Mending +20% and Prompt Prognosis. After roughly three rounds of buffs (over 20% more total healing) it's now testing okay, up notably from the prior week.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: The standout of this round of Mythic raid testing: izen reads Elemental as the overall best DPS so far — top 10 on every tested boss and top 5 on all but one. He stresses it performs regardless of damage profile, excelling on pure single-target fights (Coiled Altar, Vashnik) as well as spread/AoE ones, which he attributes to strong tuning rather than a favorable profile.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: A surprise strong performer izen didn't expect to highlight: Balance sits top-5/6 across both the spread-cleave fights and the pure single-target Coiled Altar. He frames it (with Elemental) as tuned highly regardless of profile — its multi-dotting wins on spread fights while it still ranks at the top of single target.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Arcane as one of the best-tuned DPS this cycle — very strong from 1 up to 4+ targets (Arcane Barrage splash, Prismatic Vault splash, the rebuffed reusable Arcane Missiles as an AoE button) and, crucially, also the best of the mages in single target. He explicitly places it above Frost Mage right now.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Devourer remains a consistent top performer across every tested boss, with the raid largely settled on the melee 'False Cards' build down the left side of the tree that ignores the Collapsing Star apex (Collapsing Star kept only for short M+ burst windows). izen notes it doing very well on both spread and single-target profiles.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Even after multiple nerfs this cycle, izen names Frost DK one of the best-performing raid specs — it held up through the latest round of PTR testing and stayed near the top, one of his overall highlights of the meta alongside Arms and Ret.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: One of the few melee izen highlights in a caster-favored meta: Arms posts two of the better overall results despite being surrounded by casters, thanks to ~86% boss (single-target) damage and excellent, high-uptime two-target cleave. Caveat: Arms received no tuning in the latest round — this is standing strength, not a new buff.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen repeatedly pairs Ret ('red paladin') with Arms as the top melee in this testing round — strong single-target-weighted results that keep it competitive even on the caster-favoring add fights. Like Arms, it received no changes in the latest tuning pass, so this is existing strength.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Profile-dependent for Shadow: izen has it near the top on the spread/multi-target fights (Soul Coiler, the three-target Lost Explorers) where its dots gain value, but it slips on the more single-target fights (Vashnik, Coiled Altar). A good-but-conditional read driven by damage profile more than raw tuning.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Frost Mage as good but outshone by Arcane: very strong on two-to-three-target cleave, but the closer a fight gets to pure single target the worse it does, where Arcane clearly pulls ahead. A solid cleave spec that no longer wins the mage slot outright.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Very profile-dependent: Affliction shines on the spread add fights (Soul Coiler, where izen notes it doing only ~12% boss damage and 88% on adds) but does noticeably worse in single target. He explicitly attributes its high placements to a favorable damage profile rather than across-the-board tuning.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Devastation as reasonably okay in single target but getting worse the more spread adds a fight has — the inverse of the dot/spread specs. A middling, profile-sensitive result rather than a clear winner or loser.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen groups Assassination with the consistent bottom performers across all four tested bosses — he argues it isn't a damage-profile problem but simply low, undertuned numbers relative to the rest of the field.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Fury lands in izen's consistently-poor bottom group across the tested bosses; aside from a single-target-fight cameo in top logs, he reads it as undertuned rather than merely profile-unlucky.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen lists Fire Mage among the persistent bottom performers (with Assassination, Fury, Augmentation) — consistently low results across fights that he attributes to undertuning, not damage profile.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Augmentation sits among izen's bottom performers, 'not being anything special' across the tested bosses. He caveats that Aug logs are inherently delicate to read (its contribution is buff-based), but the raw placement is poor.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Despite the recent PTR talent changes refocusing it around Wildfire Bomb, izen calls Survival's raid-testing results disappointing — it did not translate the buffs into competitive numbers this round.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen points viewers to Feral as one of the disappointing results in the testing data — a weak showing across the tested bosses.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen calls Balance one of the standout raid-testing performers of the PTR (his 'best five-ish' alongside Devourer, Arcane, Elemental and Arms), noting it has flown under the radar and been helped by Guardian and Resto Druid falling out of favor. The Stellar Amplification change nets out to a small nerf but he considers it philosophically good (capping the multi-target tab-target degeneracy); Balance stays strong.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen frames Arcane's ~2% Prismatic Bolt splash nerf as deserved: Arcane was one of the PTR all-stars in both performance and popularity and was placing top-three/top-four in the latest raid testing. He expects it to remain strong after only a light trim, with the bigger unknown being how much the Reflection of Radiance proc-rate nerf hits M+.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen again lists Elemental among the outstanding raid-testing results of the PTR (his standout group of Devourer, Arcane, Elemental, Balance and Arms), continuing to read it as one of the stronger raid DPS specs going into Season 2.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen keeps Arms in his standout raid-testing group. The cleave-nerf / Dreadnought-buff change nets out roughly neutral-to-slightly-positive (he's puzzled Blizzard talked about spreading damage off cleave but only really buffed Dreadnought), so Arms holds its strong raid standing.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen notes Devourer remains one of the most popular M+ picks and kept gapping Havoc across single-target, two-target cleave and spread-dot profiles in raid testing. The build's Collapsing Star buff / Eradicate + Annihilator nerf is a rework attempt that makes Collapsing Star usable again — especially in M+, where frequent pull-by-pull burst windows suit it — so he stays positive on Devourer for keys.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen says Unholy's AoE-focused buffs (Epidemic/Graveyard/Virulent Plague/Putrefy, ~6-7% AoE) still leave it lagging comfortably behind Frost DK, which was ahead in the raid testing and far more popular in M+ keys — he points to how hard it is to even find Unholy logs in current M+ testing.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen reads Resto Shaman as one of the more popular healers in the PTR (behind Disc and Mistweaver) and a consistent top-four in the latest raid-testing results after prior buffs. This build only slightly trims its increasingly strong healing rain (bonus rain 8s not 10s, absorb -30%) while adding riptide buffs and a big Farseer catch-up, so his raid read stays positive.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen picks Marksmanship as the DPS riser of the past week in PTR Mythic+: already top-six by popularity, now top-three over the last week and second over the last day, with visibly more top key results. He is explicit that this is 'low-profile' growth that is NOT coming from the reworked talents — even after the Explosive Shot bug fixes, Explosive Shot still comfortably outdamages Aimed Shot, so Tactical Reload and Windrunner's Quiver still are not worth taking and the intended return of Aimed Shot as the main button has not happened. The rise is essentially the flat +5% damage buff outweighing the −20% Multi-Shot nerf.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen says Mistweaver was already the popular PTR healer and that the doubled mastery value plus the tier set pushed the Rising Sun Kick fistweaving build into what he calls unhealthy territory — roughly 300k HPS over five minutes while barely touching raid frames, more so in raid than in Mythic+. Blizzard's Morning Breeze −60% is his read of Blizzard trying to tone that build down, but his conclusion is that even after the nerf Mistweaver 'remains the most promising of the healers, at the very least when it comes to Mythic+'.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen's headline tank mover: Blood DK's popularity in PTR keys has jumped from a distant second to nearly level with Prot Paladin over the last day, and he credits the round of buffs for hitting Blood's real historic weakness — damage reduction rather than self-healing. He lists Apex Dancing Rune Weapon spawns now giving 6% DR instead of 4%, +5% parry while they are out, Blood Shot adding 4% DR whenever the Blood Shield is up (about 66% uptime in his +19), and San'layn taking 3% less physical damage — alongside roughly 7-8% more damage from the Exterminate and Reaper's Mark buffs. He notes DKs have flipped to San'layn over Deathbringer as a majority pick, showing 320k DPS in a +19 versus 200k as Deathbringer, and flags only Perseverance of the Ebon Blade as a miss because of the poor talent preceding it.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen puts Brewmaster on his tank 'life support' list: it is one of the least-played tanks in PTR keys despite being a Season 1 meta pick. He rates its tier set the better of the two bottom tanks — the extra Fire damage on top of the 8% physical increase synergises with Brewmaster's own self-healing — but says the buffs handed to Blood DK and Protection Paladin were simply bigger, and that the comp-synergy explanation for its absence does not hold when Vengeance sits above it. He wants the next tuning rounds pointed here.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Guardian is izen's other tank on 'life support': near-abandoned in PTR keys even though it is one of Season 1's two most popular tanks. He calls its tier set poor — the 2-piece damage increase is weak and a longer Incarnation is not relevant given how long it already lasts — and rejects both the 'nobody plays it because it is old meta' and the 'no comp slot' explanations, since Prot Paladin, Holy Paladin and Ret are all played heavily. His read is simply that it did not get enough positive changes.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen groups Protection Warrior with Brewmaster and Guardian as the PTR's least-played tanks — an 'ill omen' three weeks out from the patch. He notes the comp-synergy excuse fails here too, since Devourer and Vengeance are both played more than Guardian and Prot Warrior despite Vengeance sharing a class with a meta DPS. He points the next rounds of tuning at this group.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Restoration Druid is the one healer izen flags across BOTH raid and Mythic+. He says it was never near the top of any raid test dating back to 2026-07-16, sitting middling-to-poor, and takes the Abundance nerf as the main cause — from 96% down to 50%, recently raised to 60%, still far short of the original. He rates its tier set genuinely powerful but mostly in raid, where the extra one-minute timing pairs with Convoke; in keys that timing matters much less. It is his top healer candidate for buffs before launch.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen splits Holy Priest by content: after its multiple PTR buffs it has been performing very well in raid testing — he cautions that the newest Mythic cuts are on short 90-second pulls and reads the ~7-minute Lost Explorers fight as the better sample — but it remains one of the traditionally worst Mythic+ healers, and he lists it (with Preservation) among the specs needing help specifically in keys.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Preservation gets the same split read as Holy Priest from izen: strong in the recent PTR raid testing after its buffs, but still one of the historically weakest Mythic+ healers and on his short list of specs that need keys-focused help before Season 2 launches. He explicitly says these two need much less help in raid than in Mythic+.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Rogue is izen's single biggest DPS question mark for Season 2, and Subtlety is part of why: all three Rogue specs sit at the bottom of both PTR Mythic+ popularity and Mythic raid-testing results, so — unlike Hunters (Marksmanship), Warlocks (Affliction) or Mages (Arcane) — there is no strong spec to fall back on inside the class. He names Rogues the number-one group he wants buffed in the three weeks of tuning before launch.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen includes Assassination in the Rogue block he calls the biggest DPS problem of the PTR: bottom-of-chart in Mythic+ popularity and high-key presence as well as in the Mythic raid tests, with no other Rogue spec performing well enough to give the class an escape route. Rogues are his top DPS buff priority for the remaining pre-launch tuning.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Outlaw completes izen's Rogue 'life support' set — bottom-tier in PTR Mythic+ popularity and high keys and in the raid testing alike. His argument is class-level: where other classes have one spec carrying them, every Rogue spec is weak at once, which is why he ranks Rogues first on his pre-launch buff list.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen's second DPS priority after Rogues is Evoker, and Devastation is the cleaner half of it. He reads it as better in raid than in Mythic+ — usually just outside the top eight and landing between middle and bottom depending on the fight — and says that over the most recent days it has been having a poor time in the highest keys being run (19s and 20s). He wants buffs that lift it to middling-to-average without creating a new top pick.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Augmentation is on izen's buff list with an explicit asterisk: he does not want it to become meta again — 'we would all be happy if Augmentation just stayed dead' — but on the results it has been outside the top picks in Mythic+ and weak in the highest keys over the past few days, better in raid than in keys. His ask is middling-to-average tuning, not a return to power.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: izen calls Havoc versus Devourer the largest in-class gap left in the PTR's bottom half: about 13 Devourer Demon Hunters are being played for every Havoc, and the divergence in keys has widened over the last four days while Devourer has also been a consistent top raid-testing performer. He says Havoc still needs a lot to close that gap, and rates it a worse problem than the other intra-class gaps (Frost vs Arcane, Fury vs Arms, BM vs Marksmanship, Demo/Destro vs Affliction, Unholy vs Frost) because those are smaller and leave a playable alternative.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: One of the ~5 melee specs repeatedly appearing higher up in the raid-testing tables (helped by fresh buffs) while most melee bunch at the bottom of a caster-favored tier.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Given 'perhaps an out' among the melee — seen higher up often enough across the tested bosses to join Arms/Frost/Enhancement/Ret as the melee that work, in a tier otherwise favoring casters.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: The runaway top tank of PTR M+: played more than every other tank spec combined, completing keys 3–5 levels higher than Blood/Guardian/Brew and 1–2 above Prot Warrior/Vengeance, with the most tank damage — the ~25–30% buff package plus talent-tree cleanup made it the most stable tank; he expects nerfs and considers it pole position for S2 meta tank.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: The turbulent riser: already top-3 in PTR M+ and, filtered to the last day of logged keys, now FIRST over Mistweaver — buffed across the board (spenders, Holy Shock, infusions via the tier set) with the crippling Holy Light mana economy actually fixed; the one weakness left is poor damage, well below Mistweaver's. Tied, he notes, to Prot Paladin's fate for the paladin slot.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Follows up his tank-mover call with the cause: Blood's Apex talent Dance of Midnight had its stacking value written into a damage-TAKEN field instead of damage-REDUCED, so every extra Dancing Rune Weapon proc was adding ~4% damage taken rather than removing it — live since Midnight launched. With that fixed on top of the 4%→6% buff he shows the swing in logs: the same Shinki +17 went from 220k to 166k damage taken per second and from 57k to 39k external HPS required, and a recent +20 puts Blood at 48k external HPS against Prot Paladin's 45k. His read is that Blood DK is now a genuine meta-tank contender for Season 2. He mentions Vengeance's fiery-brand duration bug only as a smaller comparison, not a strength call.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Frames Arms as the standout story of the Season 2 PTR: a spec that has been among the four or five least-played M+ specs every season since Legion, and — with Feral and Devastation — one of the only ones never to make a meta comp, is right now the most-picked DPS in +20s on the PTR two weeks out. He attributes the shift to Slayer overtaking Colossus rather than to Arms broadly: Tactical Edge was rebuilt to grant a guaranteed Sudden Death proc off every Colossus Smash (which accelerates Bladestorm, guarantees a Reap the Storm proc and applies Overwhelmed per Executioner stack), Slayer's Dominance went 15% to 25%, and a bug fix raised the Executioner stack cap from three to five. He shows Bladestorm's effective cooldown collapsing from 90s to roughly 24-26s in practice. Beyond raw output he credits Arms' priority damage — Slayer Strike, Mortal Strike and Execute stay single-target while the AoE runs — contrasting it with Marksmanship, which out-damages Arms overall yet loses on priority targets. The caveat he names himself: Arms brings no dispel and an Attack Power buff unlikely to matter in the ranged-caster comps it would need to join, which he calls the one real obstacle to a genuine meta slot — and he expects nerfs are possible before launch.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Frames the nerf as confirmation of strength rather than a setback: after weeks of buffs and bug fixes Blood set itself up as the most popular tank in PTR Mythic+, and what it lost is damage only — Blood Beast explosion −10%, Frenzied Bloodthirst's Death Strike/Death Coil bonus −1% per stack, Visceral Strength −2%. He calls getting nerfed this little 'a win' given the power level and stresses the recent damage-reduction gains were left untouched.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: He rates Devourer as one of the better performers across the whole testing period — consistently near the top of raid results and one of the more consistent Mythic+ DPS entries — and reads the nerf as deserved. Mechanically it lands twice: the Eradicate splash cut hits the Void-Scarred build hardest (it leans on Eradicate where Annihilator gets more from Collapsing Star), and Annihilator then eats its own trim with Final Hour's Voidful bonus persisting 6 seconds instead of 8.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: He describes Havoc as reasonably poor across the testing compared with Devourer, both in overall raid results and in Mythic+, and far less played. The combined Blade Dance / Chaos Strike / cooldown / Essence Break package nets to about 5% in both AoE and single-target-focused fights, which he calls exactly the kind of buff a weaker spec should be getting this close to release.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: He pushes back on Balance being underrated: it is currently the fifth most-played DPS spec in PTR Mythic+ and was doing well across multiple raid bosses on the strength of spread-cleave multi-dotting. The nerf is roughly 3% single target (Starsurge only) but 6-8% in AoE depending on pull size, because Moonfire, Sunfire, Starfire and Starfall all take cuts — so the larger the Mythic+ pulls, the more it costs.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: He walks through the Scintillation bug — the tier set made every Shattering Star fire as if fully empowered, including the level-one Eternity Surges Scintillation launches, bypassing that talent's 40% effectiveness — and explains the fix stacks two reductions: the 2-set's Shattering Star bonus drops from 150% to 50%, and the Scintillation multiplier now applies. Even with Deep Breath, Pyre and a 40% Disintegrate buff as compensation, he calculates the pass as roughly a 2% net nerf, which he calls weird given that Devastation was already rated poorly in both Mythic+ and raid testing.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: He totals the 33% Explosive Shot cut plus the 5% all-damage aura at roughly a 12% nerf and calls it very large. He accepts Blizzard's stated reason — a run of bug fixes kept raising Explosive Shot's damage without any tuning behind it — but notes Marksmanship had been doing quite well on PTR AoE, which is exactly what the cut targets.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: His question mark of the round: Arcane was already one of the best Mythic+ DPS specs and one of the best overall raid performers, and it still came out of the pass buffed. He dismisses the headline Arcane Blast +20% as irrelevant because Prismatic Bolt procs already replace roughly two of every three Arcane Blast casts, but flags the real one — Splintering Orbs raising the Arcane Orb bonus from 10% to 50%, which gains more value in Mythic+.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: He calls the flat 5% healing buff the more worrying of the two healer buffs: Holy Paladin is already the most-played Mythic+ healer on the PTR, and in the four days since he last checked — when it had only just edged past Mistweaver — it has gone to roughly two-and-a-half to three times Mistweaver's pick rate. His read is that it already looked strong and did not need it.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: He finds the Holy Priest buff more understandable than the Holy Paladin one but questions the diagnosis: the reason Holy Priest is not played in Mythic+ has never been that it heals for too little, and it was doing fine in raid testing — so a flat healing increase is fine but not aimed at the actual problem.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: He calls the flat 10% aura buff the most understandable change of the round: Rogues sat consistently towards the bottom for most of the fights tested regardless of damage type, and Assassination is one of the two specs getting the full 10%.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Subtlety takes the same flat 10% buff, and he singles it out as the correction of a mistake — he calls the 8% nerf it received a couple of weeks earlier 'really weird' given the spec was barely being played at all in either raid or Mythic+. He stops short of predicting it works, saying only that we will see whether the flat buffs do anything.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Outlaw gets the smallest of the three Rogue buffs at 6%, which he reads as deliberate: it was the Rogue spec doing slightly better than the others across raid testing, so it needed the least.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: He notes Shaman is the interesting target here because, unlike Rogues, Elemental was actually good — consistently strong in raid testing and consistently popular in Mythic+, often present in the top keys. The nerf goes at the hero talent rather than the spec: two 20% cuts inside Farseer, which is the de facto pick, netting roughly 5% and hurting more in AoE than single target. He reads it as reasonable given the observed power level and popularity.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: He groups Shadow with Balance as a spread-cleave outlier Blizzard appears concerned about for this raid, where several bosses put spread adds or multiple bosses up at once. The Void Volley cuts (−10%, −25% after a Tentacle slam, another 10% on Archon) come to only about a 2% nerf in pure AoE but specifically reduce the spread-cleave value that made the spec attractive on those encounters.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: After his own video calling Arms a first-in-a-decade S-tier candidate, he reads this round as Arms getting away with it. Sweeping Strikes −5% is small because much of the kit (Overpower's shockwave, Reap the Storm, Cleave, and Colossus's Concussive Slam splash) does not scale with it, and the Execute −15% costs Slayer about 3.5% but Colossus only about 0.45%. Against that, the 4-set went from 10% stacking three times to 20% stacking five — a straight buff to Colossus, which keeps Slam and its Apex-upgraded Heroic Strike. Net: roughly a 3% nerf on Slayer, effectively a buff if you fully optimise the new 4-set as Colossus.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Reads the flat 8% as a straightforward correction for one of the two tanks doing the least damage overall, noting the current top tank damage dealers are Blood DK and Prot Paladin.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Gets the same treatment as Guardian as the other lowest-damage tank — a generic damage increase he calls rather inconsequential to how the spec will play or how well it will do.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Singles it out as a rising M+ pick: strong AoE damage and, with Brewmaster fallen off and Mistweaver nerfed, the melee comp still wants a physical-damage carrier, which pushes Windwalker up the priority list. Credits the tier set, which buffs Spinning Crane Kick 120% against Rising Sun Kick 60% and so pulls the rotation onto SCK feeding Fists of Fury cooldown reduction. Caveats it heavily: arguably the squishiest DPS alongside Balance Druid, and its damage is blanket AoE with little priority-target focus, offset by a very flexible burst window off multiple Zenith charges.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Reads Mistweaver as folding: still showing decent results overall, but the shorter the window you look at, the more representation it loses to Holy Paladin and Resto Shaman. Attributes it to repeated nerfs landing at the same time as buffs to those two — specifically the 60% mastery-scaling nerf to the fistweaving Rising Sun Kick build, and an earlier pass that buffed mastery 50% but cut all healing 8%.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Has it winning the all-purpose healer slot in the generic meta comp, buffed again in the newest tuning round after several consecutive weeks of buffs while Mistweaver was nerfed. Also credits its damage-reduction package as the reason the Blood DK pairing works — Devotion Aura, Beacon of Virtue spreading 5%, and the Lightsmith armament adding another 1.3% on the tank.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Buffed repeatedly — significant Riptide healing and a large Farseer healing buff, though he flags the Farseer part as more raid-relevant. In M+ his read is comp-driven: with Mistweaver folding, Resto Shaman becomes the melee-comp healer of choice because it still brings the mastery and windfury buffs that comp wants, making a shaman-plus-monk melee group viable again.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Calls the tank meta settled and not worth debating further, with Blood DK fitting extremely well alongside Holy Paladin. His reasoning is that Blood historically fails at high keys because it can only self-heal rather than mitigate, and the paladin pairing supplies exactly the missing damage reduction — Devotion Aura, Beacon spread and the armament stacking on the tank.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Puts Balance ahead in the last-caster-slot race against Elemental — he frames it as nominally 50/50 but really more like 80/20 in Balance favour. Concedes Elemental flat AoE damage is currently slightly higher and the two damage profiles are near-identical, so he decides it on the margins: versatility as a raid buff helps both damage and defence where windfury and mastery are useless in a caster comp, and a second combat res beats a redundant bloodlust when the tank is the likeliest death.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Rates its raw M+ damage as slightly ahead of Balance Druid and its AoE profile as equally strong, but expects it to lose the last caster-comp slot anyway: windfury is dead weight in a caster group and mastery is no longer the priority stat for Devourer, Arcane, Blood or Holy Paladin, so the buffs it brings are worth less than versatility. Notes Lava Burst no longer functions as priority damage now that Voltaic Blaze turns it into six-target AoE.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Out of the caster-comp race on two counts: a recent nerf he puts at more than 10% in a single sweep, and a kit that does not benefit from the comp — physical damage, so no gain from the Devourer magical-damage debuff and none from Arcane Intellect.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Treats Arcane as the more locked-in of the two caster picks, citing its continued power level through the PTR as already-settled ground rather than something still being argued.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: The second locked-in caster-comp pick behind Arcane, valued for the magical-damage debuff the rest of the caster group scales off.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: States flatly that Brewmaster has fallen off, using it as part of the explanation for why the melee comp now has to source its physical damage from Windwalker instead.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: His headline call is "the death of Augmentation Evoker" — he says it simply will not be played in Season 2. The PTR gave it few changes and mostly hefty nerfs: duplicated Upheavals no longer knock enemies into the air, removing the mini-stuns that were real M+ value, and the Scale Commander / Wing Leader change cut the cooldown reduction on Breath of Eons — partially walked back after Blizzard judged it too deep, but still worse than the current version. On top of that its Season 2 tier set is weaker than the strong Season 1 one it replaces. He frames the upside as a meta-wide gain rather than a loss: with Augmentation gone the DPS comp opens up, because whenever Augmentation was meta it narrowed M+ compositions to a small set of casters that lined up with Arcane Intellect.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: He is explicit that this is not an M+-specific read — he calls Augmentation quite poor in the raid as well as in Mythic+, and treats its absence as freeing raid DPS slots rather than costing the raid anything.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Mentioned alongside Augmentation as being in "a similar pretty poor situation" for raid, so he counts both Evoker DPS specs as opening up raid DPS spots for other classes rather than competing for them.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Lists Devastation among the specs sitting far enough behind that ordinary tuning would not move them — it would need a larger package of help to become relevant, alongside Beast Mastery, Fury, Subtlety and Augmentation.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: His second headline rumor is the fall of Mistweaver Monk, and he tracks it through the tuning: Blizzard buffed Monk mastery back-to-back by 50% and then another 50% (he reckons ~125% compounded), which made a mastery-stacking Rising Sun Kick build very strong — Rising Sun Kick scales with mastery, the tier set adds resets, Thunder Focus Tea adds more — and then gutted the mastery scaling of Rising Sun Kick's bonus damage by 60% and gave Monk nothing afterwards, while flat-nerfing the rest of the kit throughout. He says the result is that Mistweaver is left without a proper build to play: the mastery build was cut down and the original caster build was never buffed back. Checking high keys he counts seven Monks among the 80 healers across the top-10 logs he looks at.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: He extends the Mistweaver problem to raid: the other build — the Renewing Mist caster build — is also much poorer there, both from the accumulated nerfs and because the Season 2 tier set only buffs Rising Sun Kick and drops what the Season 1 set gives, namely three bonus Renewing Mist casts per minute and a 20% Renewing Mist healing buff. He sums it up as Mistweaver being currently poor in both the raid and Mythic+.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: He has Holy Paladin establishing itself as the main healer of the season for generic all-purpose comps regardless of the DPS layout, on the back of repeated buffs across successive PTR passes and very chunky single-target healing across the board — the direct beneficiary, with Resto Shaman, of Mistweaver's collapse.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Says Holy Paladin is now much better in the raid as well, not just in Mythic+ — he treats the buff run as lifting it in both brackets.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: The answer to the melee/physical comp: buffed repeatedly through the PTR to the point that you can now pick it ahead of Mistweaver, which unlocks the whole melee package — mastery buff and Windfury from the Shaman, a Windwalker swapped in for the physical damage debuff, and the Arms Warrior's attack power buff. He frames it as the fix to a specific problem: previously you took Mistweaver for its damage debuff, but with Enhancement not strong enough to be played you never got the mastery and Windfury buffs at all. A buffed Resto Shaman supplies them itself, which is what makes the switch work.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: For raid he is more guarded: he thinks Resto Shaman would have a better chance at being just as strong as the newly-buffed Holy Paladin there, except that it goes out of mana within about five minutes of any fight.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: After the recent rogue attention — a 6% buff on top of a 3% buff about a week earlier, plus smaller ones — Outlaw is now reasonably high in picks in the higher keys and he calls it a legitimate option for melee comps. He is careful about why: it owes much of the rise to Mistweaver's nerf and to the specs that would otherwise hold the slot not being played, naming Enhancement (which he says would definitely be played if it were any stronger) and Ret Paladin. Its AoE damage is good but not the best, weaker on trash than on bosses, and its damage being mostly physical makes it a better fit than a Ret or an Unholy for a comp built around the physical debuff and Windfury.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Treats Enhancement as a spec that would definitely be played in the melee comp if it were any stronger, and isn't — it is the gap that Outlaw's buffs ended up filling.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Going through what is still undecided close to release, he says Arcane might be a lock for the traditional caster comp — the most settled of the DPS questions he runs through, ahead of Devourer and well ahead of the unresolved Elemental-versus-Balance slot.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Expects Arms in basically all of the comps, both for the attack power buff it brings and because it is doing very good damage in its own right.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Restates a call from his previous video rather than making a new one: Elemental and Balance are the 50/50 for the third slot of an Arcane/Devourer caster comp, and he still lists Elemental versus Balance among the open question marks close to release — a contender, explicitly undecided.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
