metaNotes.note: The other half of the Elemental-versus-Balance 50/50 for the third caster-comp slot, carried over from his previous video and still unresolved as of this one.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Treats Devourer as an anchor of the intellect/caster comp alongside Arcane. Ranking the open questions close to release he puts Arcane as maybe a lock for that comp and Devourer perhaps a bit less — a remark about how settled the pick is, not a knock on the spec, for which he lists no downsides.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Listed with the specs that are far enough behind that only a large set of changes, not another tuning pass, would bring them into contention.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: His Ret mentions pull both ways and the honest read is unsettled. He lists Ret among the melee physical damage dealers a comp can look at, but also as a spec that might have been played and is not, and finally puts it in the clump of melee that could become more relevant with a few more buffs — with at least three more rounds of tuning expected before the season starts, on the every-five-days cadence he counts from the patch's release.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: In the same on-the-bubble melee clump as Ret and the DK specs: not a current pick, plausibly relevant with a few more buffs. Earlier in the video he notes Havoc was the sort of option a melee comp would have reached for before the Resto Shaman buffs reshaped it.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: In the same on-the-bubble melee group; earlier he notes Unholy is a spec you might squeeze into the melee comp but that it benefits less than others from the physical/melee buff package.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: Reviewing the community 'Dummy Dome' healer test that a group of theorycrafters and streamers ran on the PTR raid healing dummy, he confirms Mistweaver as the genuine bottom of the six. He lists the accumulated causes: mastery buffed over several weeks and then reverted, a 3% aura nerf followed by a 7% aura nerf, and a Season 1 tier set worth about 15% healing being replaced by a Season 2 set worth six or seven. He does supply an asterisk — the Monk in the test showed up in markedly worse shape than the others (about 329 item level, no gems, missing enchants, gladiator gear with 700 versatility), which he estimates cost 10-15% healing — but he is explicit that correcting for it would not move the needle enough: Mistweaver was still doing badly enough that it needs buffs to be remotely competitive.
metaNotes.patchContext: Season 2 PTR — raid testing outlook (community Dummy Dome healer test)

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.note: He walks back the alarm about Restoration Druid from the same community Dummy Dome healer test, where it and Mistweaver trailed the other four by dozens of percentage points. Unlike the Monk case he argues the Druid result is largely an artefact of how it was played and geared: the tested Druid started around 325 item level and deliberately ran little or no tier set out of a conviction that the new set was bad, even crafting 292-318 blue pieces; more importantly it skipped Rampant Growth, which doubles Regrowth's heal-over-time and is worth roughly 50% more value per Regrowth cast, and it played the Season 1 pattern of heavy Rejuvenation instead of the Season 2 pattern of spreading Regrowth wide (about 10 Regrowth casts per minute where he says you want 25+, and far too few casts per minute overall for a stationary dummy fight). His conclusion is a correction rather than an endorsement: Resto Druid is nowhere near as weak as the test made it look and the panic was a knee-jerk reaction, though he allows it might still need some buff.
metaNotes.patchContext: Season 2 PTR — raid testing outlook (community Dummy Dome healer test)

metaNotes.creator: Zorthas

He immediately hedges that it would be crazy to assume Blood DK actually ends up meta, since a few changes to other specs in the coming weeks will change everything.

metaNotes.creator: Zorthas
metaNotes.note: In the same closing segment he says Holy Paladin simply does more healing than any other healer on the PTR right now. He applies the same hedge he gives Blood DK — that assuming either actually ends up meta is unwise with tuning still to come.

metaNotes.creator: Zorthas
metaNotes.note: Working from a sheet collating PTR raid-testing logs, he says Subtlety sits among the bottom five specs on essentially every boss, and that rogue occupies three of the bottom four on Lightbinded Vanguard. He argues this is not only tuning: Midnight's class design stripped the spec's low-target cleave — Subtlety lost most of its Nimble Flurry damage — and much of the new raid is two- and three-target cleave, so the spec will do low damage on those fights unless heavily overtuned elsewhere. He also notes Subtlety took an 8% nerf a few weeks earlier that surprised people.
metaNotes.patchContext: Season 2 PTR — raid outlook (recorded before the 2026-07-31 rogue aura buffs)

metaNotes.creator: Zorthas
metaNotes.note: He places Assassination alongside Subtlety among the bottom five specs on nearly every boss in the collated PTR raid-testing logs, and gives the same structural reason — rogue's low-target cleave was removed or reworked in the Midnight transition while much of the new raid is two- and three-target. He adds that the buffed Atrophic Poison raid buff does not rescue the class: environmental and untargetable damage means it delivers under 3% effective mitigation on most of the new bosses, so rogue DPS itself would have to rise significantly.
metaNotes.patchContext: Season 2 PTR — raid outlook (recorded before the 2026-07-31 rogue aura buffs)

metaNotes.creator: Zorthas
metaNotes.note: He reads Outlaw as the strongest rogue spec in public PTR raid-testing logs but frames that as faint praise — probably still a middle-of-the-pack spec at best, with a damage profile he calls undesirable for raiding, and a real commitment to gear and craft a weapon toward. He notes Outlaw has not been the raid rogue spec in modern times, the last instance being early Dragonflight on Kurog.

Lower overall than the big AoE specs but single-target priority damage on par with Arcane, and unusually strong on two-to-three target cleave, which he says several dungeons in the pool reward for long stretches. Caveat: it is on Slayer now, which he rates weaker than Colossus. He expects nearly every comp to run Arcane or Arms, often both.

metaNotes.note: Top of A+. Strong damage with two builds — Annihilator for AoE with low single target, Voidguard for single target with moderate AoE — plus Chaos Brand, Darkness and genuine tankiness, which he argues is undervalued after watching DK/DH survive content others could not in Season 1. He calls it the most likely spec to round out a group; the caveats are having to commit to one build and very high sims that could invite a raid-driven nerf.

Very good sustained five-target damage, now a consistent rather than bursty spec, decent single target and workable two-to-three target on the Farseer build, plus Skyfury as a group buff. But he pushes back on the assumption that a Druid is auto-included: he considers Elemental a slightly better version of the same role, and thinks a no-Mark season is genuinely possible.

His caveat is stability rather than ceiling — he calls it historically the most bug-prone spec and expects it to be a nerf candidate.

He disputes the claim that its single target is bad, calling it middling in competent hands with some priority damage. The reservations are practical: unwieldy, stack-dependent, with setup windows and moments of weakness, very hard to execute, and it makes groups feel unsafe. He expects pugs to avoid it and sees the case for it as fast timers rather than necessity.

His entire comp analysis is about who takes the remaining slots after Arcane.

metaNotes.patchContext: Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (which DPS specs take the comp slots)
metaNotes.note: The strongest melee spec and a lock for melee comps, but his new argument is that Arms is good enough that groups may want it even in traditional caster comps. He rates its balance between single-target and AoE as second only to Arcane, and notes it also brings Battle Shout.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.patchContext: Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (which DPS specs take the comp slots)
metaNotes.note: His current front-runner for the contested third slot. The heavily buffed Farseer version is consistent across trash and boss damage with no real profile weakness, and its damage is slightly ahead of Devourer and clearly ahead of Balance. Crucially it can buff an Arms Warrior (mastery, and Windfury even nerfed), which Devourer cannot. Caveats he names: weaker on low-pull-count dungeons like King’s Rest, nothing unique beyond raw damage, lost burst to the Ascendance nerf, and possible squishiness once key levels and item levels rise.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.patchContext: Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (which DPS specs take the comp slots)
metaNotes.note: He rates Mark of the Wild arguably the strongest raid buff in the game — 3% damage to everything plus 1.5% damage reduction, which he likens to a Battle Shout and Chaos Brand combined plus half a Devotion Aura — and its mass AoE in very large pulls as potentially top of the table. The weakness is boss damage: on the AoE build M+ pushes it toward, single-target is poor, which he calls more problematic than Elemental’s equivalent gap, and there are not many pulls big enough to pay off its ceiling.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.patchContext: Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (which DPS specs take the comp slots)
metaNotes.note: He argues Devourer’s stock is falling, and the reason is structural rather than tuning: its 3% magic-damage raid buff loses about half its value the moment an Arms Warrior is in the group, because physical damage gets nothing from it. Its own damage he places below both Arms and Elemental. He still lists Arcane/Elemental/Devourer as the highest-odds trio if Arms stays confined to melee comps — so the read is contingent, not a write-off.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.patchContext: Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (which DPS specs take the comp slots)
metaNotes.note: He reports Windwalker doing top damage with rising popularity, helped by Resto Shaman displacing Mistweaver in melee comps and wanting the physical damage debuff. The asterisk he repeats is survivability: still "made of paper" this patch, so the question at higher keys is staying alive rather than whether the damage is there.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.patchContext: Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (which DPS specs take the comp slots)
metaNotes.note: Named only as the distant fallback ranged pick. He measures the gap by PTR play rate — Shadow is the next-most-played ranged spec after Balance and Elemental but sits roughly 1.5 times below them and about three times below Elemental, which he presents as evidence the supposed alternative is not really in the conversation.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.patchContext: Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (which DPS specs take the comp slots)
metaNotes.note: Referenced as the spec whose loss of value opened the melee-comp healer slot for Resto Shaman — he treats Mistweaver falling out as an established fact underpinning the rest of his comp reasoning rather than an open question.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.patchContext: Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (which DPS specs take the comp slots)
metaNotes.note: He has it taking the healer slot Mistweaver vacated, and specifically because it is strong in melee comps — which in turn props up Windwalker, since a melee comp wants the physical damage debuff alongside it.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.patchContext: Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (the risk case: what could stop each meta-candidate spec from actually being meta)
metaNotes.note: He treats Blood as the settled staple tank of the season after its buffs overtook Protection Paladin, and calls it one of the best versions of the spec in several expansions. The named risk is the old one: its mitigation is self-healing rather than avoidance or absorbs, so very high keys where auto-attack damage outpaces the self-heal remain the ceiling. He deliberately deflates the popular version of that worry, pointing at logs where the tank drops below half health only a handful of times in a 28 and never below 29%, and notes a Holy Paladin pairing would patch it further with flat damage reduction rather than more healing.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.patchContext: Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (the risk case: what could stop each meta-candidate spec from actually being meta)
metaNotes.note: The most-played keystone healer, with what he considers the strongest single-target healing toolkit of any healer bar a Holy Priest's Serenity, plus real utility for this season — poison dispel in a poison season, Freedom against snares, and Sacrifice/Blessing of Protection as externals — and good personal survivability. The weakness he singles out is even AoE healing: the kit is single-target by construction, so spread rot damage is only partly covered through beacons. He compares the failure mode to Discipline Priest in an earlier season, where excellent spot saves still capped the key level the healer could sustain.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.patchContext: Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (the risk case: what could stop each meta-candidate spec from actually being meta)
metaNotes.note: The clearest positive read in the video — he says there is no real danger of Arcane falling out of the meta. It is strong on both trash and single target rather than trading one for the other, brings Arcane Intellect and Bloodlust, and gained meaningful durability from the change that spreads a portion of damage taken over time and restores Mirror Image's role as a defensive, which he rates highly against one-shots and small burst windows.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.patchContext: Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (the risk case: what could stop each meta-candidate spec from actually being meta)
metaNotes.note: He is positive on the spec in isolation — tanky enough, Rallying Cry plus single-target and AoE stuns, better boss damage than the other contenders even if not matching Arcane — and locates the entire risk in composition rather than power. In a caster/intellect group Arcane Intellect is wasted on Arms and a Devourer would instead buff two casters by 3% each, so Arms can lose the slot without being outclassed. He notes the fallback is solid: in a melee composition he sees no danger of it being displaced.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.patchContext: Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (the risk case: what could stop each meta-candidate spec from actually being meta)
metaNotes.note: Damage is not the concern — the tier set's heavily buffed Spinning Crane Kick keeps its trash damage strong and he considers it fine on bosses too, so unlike other specs it does not fall off when target count drops. Survivability is the risk. He calls Windwalker traditionally among the squishiest specs and points out that where other historically fragile specs were given baseline durability over the years, monks lost tools instead, leaving Fortifying Brew and Touch of Karma as thin cover for a melee spec at the key levels the season will reach.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.patchContext: Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (the risk case: what could stop each meta-candidate spec from actually being meta)
metaNotes.note: He puts Balance at the edge of the contender group: its large-pull AoE is among the best in keys and enough on its own to argue an S-tier slot, but single-target and boss damage are much weaker, and the AoE itself is conditional on pull size. His worked example is the dot-application ramp — several global cooldowns spent seeding Moonfire and Sunfire before the spec starts actually doing damage — which pays off on big pulls and is wasted on small, split ones. Playing the AoE-focused hero build to get that ceiling costs single-target damage in turn.

metaNotes.creator: izen (Izenhart)
metaNotes.patchContext: Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (the risk case: what could stop each meta-candidate spec from actually being meta)
metaNotes.note: He rates Elemental the caster that most consistently gets closest to Arcane, with its AoE significantly buffed into the default choice and its real strength being consistency across single target, cleave and AoE alike. Two things could cost it the slot: it has no short-window burst — he contrasts it with Arcane or Arms lining up cooldowns on a spawn wave, where Elemental can only place Earthquake and chain-cast — and it is squishy, with a single 40% mitigation on a 90-second cooldown as its main defensive. He adds that much of its group value is contingent, since Windfury and Mastery matter far less if an Arms Warrior is not in the composition.

metaNotes.creator: Zorthas
metaNotes.patchContext: 12.1 PTR — Season 2 outlook: a reliability caution about his own current Arcane placement, not a new placement (complements, not replaces, his 08-09 M+ tier-list read)
metaNotes.note: He reviews his own past Arcane Mage placements and finds an uncomfortable pattern: he had it S tier before three of the last four seasons and C tier before the fourth — and the C-tier season was the only one in which Arcane was actually meta. He draws the general lesson that early tier lists are usually wrong because tuning and strategy development move a spec's perception after the season opens, then applies it to now, calling Arcane Mage's current position a very risky spot given that he and every other tier-list maker have again placed it high. The clip ends mid-sentence before he names the tier, so the placement itself is not on the record here. Recorded mixed: this is a caution about the confidence of the high consensus placement, not a claim that the spec is weak.
